Yew's lich lords (two spawners at (987–1001, 725–787), radius 30, 8 each): one zone #19 "E of Yew" 576 × 476 with 26 spawners and 218 deaths → #117 "liches and lich lords, E of Yew" 112 × 156, deadly, fight 4,673 at the worst place, promised 4,694 at a place; (900, 700) itself is bear ground 90 tiles west of them, a lich lord there is a wanderer while it is there. Build 97 → 117 ms off the loop (the fight raster +13 ms, 1,300 rings traced on the first build); JSON 1,169 → 1,398 KB.
- *Dials (`bot-zones.json`):* `JoinGap` 8, `ZoneMostTiles` 192, `StrayBeyond` 16, `ObservedSlack` 8, `TownsClear` true. If the wide "Outdoors" zones (300 × 300 of discs and sightings) still refuse too many roads: `LooseRadius` 12 → 8, `ObservedMargin` 1 → 0.
- *Counted:* `Zones:` gains "Accuracy: N zones of the land's attackers (M of wanderers) paint Xk tiles as patrol or fringe (Yk of patrol); the largest #id label at W×H tiles (…); A attackers alive, P a thousand tiles of patrol; T town squares under a patrol or fringe; G guarded cells kept clear of C". `/api/zones` gains `accuracy {landZones, strayZones, paintedTiles, patrolTiles, attackers, townsInside, guardedKept, largest {id, label, width, height, tiles}}`; the dashboard's danger bar shows "local N land zones (M wandering) · Xk tiles · largest #id W×H · P attackers/1k tiles · T towns under paint" (click selects the largest); zones carry `stray` and `power.declared`. `Getting about:` gains the road check's samples and milliseconds.

Deaths promotion (6 in 24 h → deadly) now lands on 50–100k-tile zones; it only costs 300 a node where the cell's fight is ≥ 3× the walker. The record of deaths (`BotQuad.Muscle`, 7.65 M of the 10.3 M road refusals on 388) is not the zones' and decays on its own clock.

**02.10.2026 · build 389 (written by Fable) · What the guards of a town will and will not do, read from the engine**
- *Patrick (02.10, 00:20):* "If a bot is beaten on the road and understands it cannot win the fight, it must run to town, because the guards are supposed to kill hostile creatures that fight within the town limits."
- *Read in `Projects/UOContent/Regions/GuardedRegion.cs`, `Mobiles/Guards/BaseGuard.cs`, `WarriorGuard.cs`, `Misc/Notoriety.cs`, `Server/Mobiles/Mobile.cs` (era UOR, `core.expansion` in `modernuo.json`; `AllowReds => Core.AOS` is false):*
  - A guard is spawned for a **guard candidate** only: `IsGuardCandidate(m)` is "alive, not a guard, not blessed, not invulnerable, and `m.Criminal` or a murderer". Nothing in the region looks at whether a thing is a monster. 31 creature types are `AlwaysMurderer` (brigands, evil mages, savages, juka, plague spawn, energy vortices) and are candidates on sight; none of the island's killers — reaper, giant spider, giant serpent, orc, ettin, gargoyle, troll, lich lord, ogre, wisp — is one.
  - A creature becomes **criminal** by harming an innocent: `Mobile.DoHarmful` → `IsHarmfulCriminal` → `Notoriety.Compute(creature, bot) == Innocent` → `CriminalAction` sets `Criminal` for `ExpireCriminalDelay` (2 min). A bot is innocent to a creature unless it has struck that creature within `AggressorInfo.ExpireDelay` (2 min): `MobileNotoriety` answers `CanBeAttacked` through `CheckAggressor(source.Aggressors, target)`. So a serpent that bites a bot which never swung at it is criminal from its first bite; a serpent that bites a bot which swung back is not criminal for that bite, and the region never learns of it.
  - The region remembers a criminal act for 15 s (`m_GuardCandidates`, from `OnAggressed` when the *victim* stands in the region and from `OnCriminalAction` when the *criminal* does). Then either a human NPC of the town within 8 tiles calls the guards at once (the "fakeCall"), or anybody saying a sentence with the *guards* keyword (0x0007) within 14 tiles calls them: `GuardedRegion.OnSpeech` → `CallGuards`. A `WarriorGuard` teleports to the candidate and kills it outright (`guards.instantKill`, default true, not overridden in `modernuo.json`), no corpse, no loot. `OnEnter` checks murderers only.
- *What that means for bots.* `BotMobile.OnDamage` squares every struck bot up to its attacker unconditionally ("hitting back is a reflex"), and the engine's combat timer swings within a tenth of a second when the weapon is ready; one swing — hit or miss, `BaseWeapon.OnSwing` → `HarmfulCheck` → `DoHarmful` — puts the bot in the creature's aggressors for two minutes. A bot that then runs to town and calls "Guards!" gets nothing: its attacker is not criminal for hitting the bot that hit it. The honest lever is the player's, and it has two halves: **say "guards" standing in the town with the thing on you, and do not swing at it.**
- *Decision (`BotHaven`, new; `BotBolt` third constructor; `BotFugitive.ToTown`; `BotDefender`; `BotMobile.OnDamage`):*
  - A bot that cannot win — the fugitive's own judgement (threat over half of what it has left on the Failing rung, over 1.5× on the Hunted rung under 70 % health, `BotFugitive.Propose`), or the defender's refusal to hit back because the odds where it stands are past `BotThreat.Tolerance` (`BotDefender.Propose`, Outmatched, which until now raised a cry and kept the errand) — runs for the nearest guarded town when that is realistic (`BotHaven.Choose`): the guarded edge of one of the three nearest reachable towns along the straight line (`BotHaven.Nearest`, the engine asked every 8 tiles, one stride inside the first guarded tile, the reach map asked), within `Reach` 300 tiles, under `MostSeconds` 90 s at the runner's own pace now (200 ms a step afoot running, 100 mounted, double at a walk when out of breath), the pursuer no quicker than that pace unless the town is within `NearTiles` 40 (the island's killers step at 0.25–0.3 s, air elementals and wisps at 0.2, `npc-speeds.json`; a bot running afoot is never outpaced, a bot out of breath always is), and the straight road asking no more than ×1.5 what the bot brings (`BotDanger.Road`, 388's deadlier-landings rule for the whole road). Not from under the ground; not for a bot in a company, which is its own refuge; not from a caster (Patrick: fight to the end); not for a bot that has run `MostRepeats` times lately, which stands as before.
  - The run (`BotBolt.RunForTown`): one walk to the haven over the planner's road, priced for the walker; inside guarded ground, with the thing still on the bot (`Pursued`: a creature within 24 tiles with the bot for its combatant, or a blow inside 4 s), `DoSpeech("Guards! Help!", [0x0007], …)` every `GuardsEveryMs` 3 s — the same call a player's client sends — and on to the town's square so the chase crosses the town's own people; `Done` when nothing follows, `Failed("could not shake")` at `HavenMs` 150 s: the run is under 90 s, and a creature the bot struck before it ran is innocent to it again two minutes after the last swing, so its next blow in the town is the criminal one. A refused road turns the run back into the plain flight (`Bend`, counted).
  - **No swing on the run, and none from a bot outmatched that has not yet struck its attacker** (`BotBolt.HoldsSwing`, `BotMobile.OnDamage`): the reflex is held when the bot holds a run for a town, and when `BotThreat.Decide` says Outmatched and the bot does not stand in the creature's aggressors (`BotHaven.Aggressed`, the engine's own list). A bot that has judged it cannot win keeps its hands down so that the guards keep their claim. The odds are computed once per blow where they were computed before; a bot hit by another bot, by a war's enemy, is unchanged.
- *Counted, in the mending line (`BotBolt.Describe`, after the flights):* "runs for a town: N begun, N reached guarded ground, N calls for the guards (N of them while the runner stood in its pursuer's aggressors, which the guards cannot answer), N pursuers cut down by the guards, N died on the way, N could not shake it in the town inside 150s, N swings held by a bot outmatched that had not struck its attacker (on); towns weighed as a refuge for a beaten bot: N asked, N chosen, N with no guarded town within 300 tiles, N further than 90s of running, N against a pursuer quicker than the runner beyond 40 tiles, N over a road asking more than the runner brings, N turned back to the plain flight for a refused road". In the fugitive's part: "N runs for a town offered by the defender to a bot that could not win where it stood"; in `Arms:`: "N answered with a run for a town by a bot outmatched where it stood". Per run: "X runs for Trinsic from (x, y) …", "X reached Trinsic at (x, y) after Ns of running …", "X's pursuer Y was cut down by the guards of Trinsic". Dials in `bot-mend.json`: `FleeToTown`, `FleeTownReach`, `FleeTownSeconds`, `FleeTownNear`, `FleeTownMs`, `FleeHoldsSwing`.
- *Measured on 388 (00:14–09:15):* 721 deaths, 1,042 flights (737 early), 96 died running, 113 "could not shake" (trolls 17, ettins 11, spiders 8, harpies 6, vines 6), 213 clean; the median flight was from a threat 2.3× what the bot had left. 360 of the 721 deaths fell within 300 tiles of a town's square (half), 121 within 200; of the 96 flight deaths, 33 began within 300 tiles of one. The coordinator's point 4 (flight path share 94.9 % after 04:09, local to Katra and Falk at (1800–1900, 2800–3000) SE of Trinsic and Elandor in Covetous): Katra's and Falk's flights were eighteen-tile legs through the Trinsic jungle from ettins, snakes and vines, each leg a partial plan, 22 and 18 of them; both stood 150–250 tiles from Trinsic's guarded edge, which the run now takes as one road; Elandor is underground, where no town is weighed. Watch the flight path share with `Runs` against `FellOnWay`.
- *Watch after deploy:* `Reached` against `Runs` (the run is realistic if most reach); `GuardKills` against `GuardsCalled` and `CallsBlind` — if nearly every call is blind, the first reflex swing is still landing before the run begins and the next step is to hold the swing on the first blow for every bot the odds say is outmatched *before* `Decide` (it already is: `SwingsHeld`); `FellOnWay` against `Fell`; `UnshakenInTown`; the flight path share; deaths within 300 tiles of a town by `deaths.py`.
- *Risk:* a run for a town brings the thing to the town's edge; a creature that is not criminal there is not killed there, and a bot at the square with a troll on it that the guards will not answer stands and takes it for up to 150 s unless the troll loses interest (`UnshakenInTown` says how often). The held swing costs the outmatched bot the damage it would have done on the move to a thing several times its size, which is little; it costs nothing to a bot that already struck. `dial BotBolt.HoldsSwing false` restores the reflex; `dial BotHaven.Running false` the plain flight.

**02.10.2026 · build 389 (written by Fable) · Any fighter's company for a square where bots lately died, and the ground's closures lifted with it**
- *Patrick (02.10, 00:20):* "I don't see bots gathering in companies and going to the squares where others died, to clear them and protect other bots on the road."
- *Measured on 388 (00:14–09:15):* 721 deaths, 500 of bots alone, in the same cells all night — (1300, 1400) 32, (900, 700) 25, (1700, 2500) 23, (1800, 3000) 22; 408 quadrants took a death, 149 of them two or more, 24 five or more ((1365, 1485) 13, (2775, 855) 10, (855, 495) 10). What was raised: 59 patrols (`BotPatrol`: captains and guild heads only, 3,349 of 5,078 asks refused "too few free bots near" — two free able allies within 40 tiles — and aimed at `BotPeril.Worst`, the blow count, not the dead); 15 of the Baron's musters, 1 marched, 14 "came up N of 6; not in the square" (`BotHarrower`: one bot on the island may call one, and it waits for a head count); 43 guild harrows offered for a guild's own dire squares (`BotReeve`: needs a guild with ground). 9 quadrants were harrowed all night, all by Cedric's one march at 07:48. Meanwhile `BotBreaker` closed 94 boxes to single bots that died twice on a piece of ground and `BotBarred` quarantined 90 killing fields (14 in force at 09:15, 813,622 choices turned), and nothing lifted either but the clock. **Every company that clears ground stood behind a gate — a rank, a guild, a Baron — and the ground stood behind all three.**
- *Decision (`BotClearer`, new, registered with the squads; `BotHarrow` as a clearing):* any fighter — not a producer, not a neutral trader, not a healer (levied as the medic), not a novice under `LeastSkill` 50 in its main skill, not in a company, hurt, or standing off a muster that failed — is offered the square where `LeastDeaths` 2 or more died, the last inside `RecentMs` 2 h, within `Reach` 600 tiles, reading at or below `BotQuad.Wanted`: **the ones on a road between towns first** (`BotRoadbook`: within `RoadWidth` 30 of a drawn road's waypoints, remembered ten minutes), then the most dead, then the latest. The square must be reachable, not harrowed already (`BotHarrow.Taken`), not cleared within the hour, and not beyond the Baron's own test (`BotHarrower.Takeable`: damned ground wants the grandmasters; ground whose fight is `BotPeril.Overwhelm` 3× a levy's company is left to the Baron — the lich lord at (900, 700) reads 28,730 and is left). **The strength fit:** the square asks the larger of the record of what has killed there (`BotQuad.Muscle`) and what stands there now (`BotPeril.Hostility`, 10 s cells); the bots within the levy's 200 tiles of the muster must bring `ClearFit` 1.25 times it (`BotHarrow.SupplyStrength`, the callable ones, `TooWeak` otherwise) and be at least `Least` 3. At most `MostAtOnce` 3 clearings stand at once. The company is the harrow's — the levy that puts work down, the muster, the march, the box of 75 walked until `Quota` 20 corpses or `CapMs` 30 minutes, the nine quadrants set to nothing — with three changes for a clearing: it musters where its leader stands when outside a town (the Baron's muster is the population's home; a Trinsic fighter would have called at Britain), it is sized by strength (`_wanted` = bodies of the leader's strength the square asks, up to a company) and **marches the moment that strength stands at the muster with three bodies, not at a head count**, and short of the strength at the bell it does not go (`ClearUndermanned`, the leader stands off ten minutes). Priced at `ClearPrior` 150 a minute, `Unpaid` so the ledger cannot refuse it for earning nothing.
- *Decision (lifting; `BotBarred.Lift`, `BotBreaker.LiftGround`, in `BotHarrow.Finish`):* when a harrow — the Baron's, a guild's or a clearing — ends with its ground cleared, every quarantine whose box holds the square or lies within the box walked, and every box closed to any bot that holds the square, is lifted and said so; `BotPeril.Cleared` and `BotQuad.Cleared` as before. The standing bars (Patrick's four) are never lifted.
- *Counted, in `The island:` (new tail "clearings: …", `BotClearer.Describe`):* "N fighters asked (N answers went to bots that are not fighters): N offered a square where 2 or more died in the last 120 minutes (N of them on a road between towns), N novices, N already in a company, N too hurt, N standing off a muster that failed, N asked with 3 clearings already standing, N found no such square within 600 tiles, N squares passed over as cleared within the hour, N as being harrowed already, N as unreachable or beyond the Baron's own test, N asks found the bots within call bringing less than ×1.25 what the square asks, N fewer than 3 within call; N marched, N emptied their ground, N ran out of time on it, N came up short at the bell, N things killed, **N deaths on cleared ground within 60 minutes**; N quarantines and N closed boxes lifted with the ground". The Baron's line carries the same clearing counters after its own; `Getting about:` "… N lifted by a company that cleared the ground" on the quarantines; `Will:` "… N lifted by a company that cleared the ground" on the boxes; `The island:` "N harrowed (N deaths on a square within 60 minutes of its clearing)". Per clearing: "X the Warrior has been offered the first clearing on this shard: (x, y), where N have died, on a road between towns; the ground asks N of strength and N stands within call", then the harrow's own lines ("is calling for volunteers … to harrow", "is marching N of the N called", "has been harrowed"). Dials in `bot-squad.json`: `Clearings`, `ClearReach`, `ClearDeaths`, `ClearRecentMs`, `ClearLeastSkill`, `ClearFit`, `ClearExpects`, `ClearRoadWidth`.
- *The coordinator's points 1–3 and 5:* (1) Yew's lich lord and gargoyles: a clearing asks the ground's strength first and is not offered where everybody within call brings less than ×1.25 of it, nor where the Baron's own `Overwhelm` test refuses; the two-and-three-bot companies at Yew are bands and patrols, not clearings. (2) Bands losing their quarry while gathering (46 of 198) and (3) no healer within 150 tiles to levy (613) are the band's and the levy's, not this patch's; the clearing's medic comes from the harrow's own `Take(Medic, 1)` within 200 tiles, so the same shortage will show as clearings without a medic — left to the next fixer. (5) Trinsic ×2.45: the squares the measurement names ((1700, 2500), (1800, 3000), (1800, 2900), (1600, 2700)) are exactly the ones the clearer ranks first when they lie on the Trinsic–Britain road.
- *Watch after deploy:* `Offered` against `Asked` and the named refusals (`TooWeak` and `Quiet` are the two that should dominate if nothing marches); `ClearMarches` against `ClearUndermanned`; `ClearEmptied` + `ClearTimedout` against `DiedAfterClearing` (a cleared square that keeps killing is the measure that this is theatre); `QuarantinesLifted` and `BoxesLifted`; the top death cells by `deaths.py` after three hours; deaths at `enlist` (295 on 388) — the levy puts bots in a company, and a company's deaths are counted there.
- *Risk:* the levy presses up to a company off their work for every clearing called (three at once at most); `Resting` and `Taken` bound the churn, `Enough` counts the cap. A clearing marched against the record alone (what killed there has wandered off) walks an empty box for its clock — `ClearTimedout` says so, and the `Hostility` half of the ask is what keeps a company from marching into a lich lord that is still there. `dial BotClearer.Running false` turns it off; `dial BotHarrow.ClearFit 1.5` asks more.

**02.10.2026 · build 389 (written by Fable) · A delivery is a meeting: the buyer comes to the carrier, or both go to safe ground**
- *Patrick (02.10, 00:20):* "Today I saw a couple of times the customer of the goods running away from the supplier. The result of the trade must be that they meet: either they walk towards each other, or they meet on safe ground."
- *Measured on 388 (00:14–09:15, `took on deliver` matched to its ending):* 654 deliveries ended, 555 handed over, 58 failed, 28 dropped, 13 put down; median 26 s from taking to the hand, but 195 over a minute, 108 over two, 39 over five (Faelar after Dorin 549 s, Uldreth after Balgrim 698 s; Liriel after Dorin 304 s and dropped, Berengar after Norbert 184 s and dropped). The buyer meanwhile took up a prowl, a hunt, a tame, a counter and kept going (the buyer's own `took on` lines inside the chase). The "could not catch up in 8 minutes" ending fired 0 times in nine hours and 0 on 387, because the auction took the carrier off the chase first — `Late` is a counter that cannot trip. The carrier followed the buyer by its body (`BotDoing.Walk(map, buyer, …)`, `BotDeliver`; `BotHaul` the same inside `NearTiles` 40 for `ChaseMs`) and the buyer was never told. The traders' line: 382 hauls, 304 finished, 74 failed, 3,390 wants passed over for "the buyer on deadly ground".
- *Decision (`BotRendezvous`, new; `BotMeet` deed and `BotMeeter` proposer; `BotDeliver`, `BotHaul`):* a carrier within `CallTiles` 60 of its buyer calls the meeting (`BotRendezvous.Call`, said again every beat while near; one a buyer at a time, a second carrier follows as before, `Doubled`). The buyer's proposer, on the free rung, offers it `BotMeet`: `Pressing` (the carrier is a screen away now, the next review may be half a minute off), `Summons` (through a steadfast hold; the seam is put down and taken up again), `Resumes`, `Unpaid` (the buyer pays here; the ledger cannot refuse it for earning nothing), `Made` = the goods received at the want's offer, claimed at `Prior` 150 a minute for a minute. The buyer walks towards the carrier (`BotDoing.Walk` after its body — both follow each other and close), stands when within `BotHandover.MeetTiles` and lets the carrier's own beat hand over; gives the meeting `MeetMs` 3 min and stands `WaitMs` 20 s beside a carrier that hands nothing over. **Safe ground:** when either of the two stands in a hostile or deadly patrol zone or on a square whose record asks more than it brings (`BotRendezvous.Unsafe`), the meeting place is the nearest guarded ground to the point between them (`BotHaven.Nearest`, a town's edge) within `SafeReach` 160 of both, and both walk there — the carrier waits at the place, the buyer comes to it; with no guarded ground near enough they still walk towards each other, which is at least not a chase. A bot in a company is not offered the meeting; the carrier follows as before. The carrier's endings tell the registry: handed over → met; the delivery dropped, the haul's line struck, nothing to hand → gone.
- *Counted, in `The market:` (after the deliveries, `BotRendezvous.Describe`):* "meetings: N called by a carrier within 60 tiles (N of them moved to guarded ground for the ground one stood on), N taken up by the buyer, N met with the goods handed over, N missed (N the buyer waited 3 minutes and the carrier never came, N stood together 20s and nothing changed hands, N the carrier gave the delivery up first, N the carrier fell out of call for 45s), N calls for a buyer already meeting another carrier"; on the deliveries: "N deliveries called a meeting once within 60 tiles of the buyer, N beats spent going to or waiting at a guarded meeting place". Per meeting: "X is 41 tiles from Y with 12 Raw Ribs and calls the meeting: they walk towards each other" / "… at (x, y), guarded ground, since where they stand is not safe". Dials in `bot-market.json`: `Meetings`, `MeetingCallTiles`, `MeetingMs`, `MeetingWaitMs`, `MeetingSafeReach`, `MeetingExpects`.
- *Watch after deploy:* `Met` against `Arranged` and `TakenUp` (the buyer must take it up: if `TakenUp` lags `Arranged`, the meeting is losing the buyer's auction and `MeetingExpects` wants raising); the delivery durations by the same matching (median 26 s, p90 196 s on 388 — the p90 is the number to move); `Late` stays 0 and means nothing; `StoodApart` (the two together and no exchange: a pack full, a buyer that cannot pay — `BotHandover`'s refusals say which); `meet` in the dashboard's kinds under 80 %.
- *Risk:* a buyer pressed off steadfast work for a minute: the hold is lifted by `Summons` and the work taken up again, counted in `Resolve:` as put down and taken up; a buyer at a counter or a shop shift walks a screen away and back. A meeting on guarded ground sends both to a town's edge up to 160 tiles off — further than the chase would have been when the buyer was walking towards the carrier anyway; the alternative was the hand-over on ground one of them should not stand on. `dial BotRendezvous.Running false` restores the follow.

**02.10.2026 · build 389 (written by Fable) · Not done, and why**
- The band's gathering losing its quarry (46 of 198) and the healers nobody can levy (613 companies without one, 43 levied): the band's and the levy's; said above, left to the next fixer. The patrol's "too few free bots near" (3,349 of 5,078 asks, 40 tiles): `BotPatrol` is the captain's offer and `BotSweep` goes to the blow count; the clearing is the company for the dead and reaches 200 tiles for its levy, so the patrol is left as it is.
- The first reflex swing before a flight is chosen still blinds the guards for two minutes for a bot the odds call Fight (an ettin or a troll at 1.0–1.4× a bot); the held swing is for Outmatched only, by the same `Decide` the fight uses. If `CallsBlind` dominates `GuardsCalled` after deploy, the next honest step is to hold the swing of any bot whose health is under the early flight's gate.
- *Code:* `BotCombat/BotHaven.cs` (new), `BotCombat/BotBolt.cs`, `BotCombat/BotFugitive.cs`, `BotCombat/BotRescuer.cs`, `BotCombat/BotCry.cs`, `BotPopulation/BotMobile.cs`, `BotMend/BotMendConfig.cs`; `BotSquad/BotClearer.cs` (new), `BotBaron/BotHarrow.cs`, `BotMovement/BotBarred.cs`, `BotWill/BotBreaker.cs`, `BotQuad/BotQuad.cs`, `BotPopulation/BotBeat.cs`, `BotSquad/BotSquadModule.cs`, `BotSquad/BotSquadConfig.cs`; `BotMarket/BotRendezvous.cs` (new), `BotMarket/BotDeliver.cs`, `BotTraders/BotHaul.cs`, `BotMarket/BotMarketModule.cs`, `BotMarket/BotMarket.cs`, `BotMarket/BotMarketConfig.cs`. No engine file and no configuration file changed; every dial has its code default. `BotZones`, `BotRest` and `BotGrowth` untouched.
- *Measure after deploy, over three hours and by town:* `python roads4-tools/measure_roads.py <log> <HH:MM:SS>` and `python opus386/deaths.py <log> <HH:MM:SS>` for deaths, cells and flights; the mending line's "runs for a town" and "towns weighed" tails; `The island:`'s "clearings:" tail and "N deaths on a square within 60 minutes of its clearing"; `The market:`'s "meetings:" tail and the delivery-duration matching above (median, p90, over-five-minutes). **02.10.2026 · build 389 (written by Fable) · The poor: the keep lifted, hunting for gold, the mint on heads, the pile before the counter, the price of a death — and the traders' own ribs**

- *Patrick's choice (02.10, relayed by the coordinator ~01:00):* "Patrick picked his options from your poverty-388.md. Implement **options 1, 2, 3 and 4**. Under 4 I also gave him your option 5 (reclaim a corpse holding ≥ 20 gp, and price death fully in the ledger), so that is in too. O1: the guild keep goes from 300 to 800. Cap `BotGuilds.Stand`. Dues are taken only above the keep. O2: poor hunters rank quarry by the gold a kill actually pays, and prowl to zones that pay. O3: half of the city mint goes from fairs to automatic bounties on the kinds that kill bots, split like spoils. The mint total does not change. O4: consumables come from bots or from the glut before NPCs. A mage's casts are capped by the quarry's gold. Option 5 is part of this." Standing rules kept: poor bots hunt; nothing is handed out; the mint is unchanged.
- *Measured before the change (`poverty-388.md`; 386 = 7.47 h, 362 online bot-h; 388 = 9 h overnight, ~51 online):*
  - 55 % of 83 economic bots under 100gp, median 80 (388 at 09:15: median 95, 48 purses, 18,151gp). **Not one guild member of any class above 300gp** (Treasuries: "0 of 15 above the 300gp keep, the richest 299gp"); every bot above 300 is guildless (Trader median 508, Architect 2,350, Baron 8,315).
  - `BotGuilds.Stand` moved 58,229gp richest-first down to the 300 keep in 388's nine hours (113,213 "could not"); dues took 22,170gp. The chest paid 10,119gp of supplies against 9,937gp of dues on 386: a pass-through to the NPC counters.
  - Hunting: solo corpse gold 3.1gp a corpse on 386 (141 of 151 kills were grazers at nought), 19.5gp on 388 after the aggressive-first rule (930 corpses, 18,139gp); company splits 36.7gp a corpse, 3–5 heads (43,360gp over 1,810 splits on 388). Loot credited as "made" (hunt 45,623 vs coin 4,911) is glutted at ×0.10.
  - Sinks: NPC purchases 143gp a bot-hour on 386 (82,486gp on 388), 60 % consumables; deaths 2.85 a bot-hour on 386 (1.56 on 388), pocket on the corpse 46gp a bot-hour, 7.5 % reclaimed (27 reclaims, 1,271 of 16,835gp); lessons 7, beds 3. The mint: 22,000 in 7.5 h, 13,700 of it at four fairs to the ten shopkeepers (339gp a shift); bounties paid 0.
  - Traders: 38 hauls failed "could not say the want at the bank" on 388, all raw ribs, 48 % of every failed haul (haul share 79.8 % against 88.6 % without them); the market refused 0 wants for want of money and held 37 of 512.

**O1 — the keep (`BotEstate.Keep` 300 → 800; `BotGuilds.StandShare` 0.25; `BotDues.Pay` only above the keep; `BotProvision.BandageShare` 0.5 → 0.25).**
- The keep stands at the gear purse, above the horse (600) and the armourer's reserve (400), which nobody has reached since the wipe (0 horses). A call on a mate takes at most a quarter of what it holds above the keep; what the cap withholds is counted (`CappedGold`, Guilds line: "Ngp left with their holders by the 25 % cap on a call above the 800gp keep"). Dues are clipped to what the member holds above the keep (`UnderKeep`, `UnderKeepGold` in the Treasuries line: "N held back (Mgp) for a member at or under the keep"). `BotEstate.Keep` is already in `bot-estate.json` (`Keep`); the live file does not name it, so the code default rules.
- Mitigation inside the option: with the stand capped and dues dry until members pass 800, the chest route starves too; the entry bar for bandages falls to a quarter of the kit so the companies — the island's whole income — stay open to the poor. `Bottles`, `AmmoShare`, `Casts` unchanged.
- Risk: fewer funded enlists (watch `BotProvision` Unfunded in the Delving line, "supplies: ... could not pay N"); the hall fund (`BotEstate.Spare`) reads members above 800 and will read 0 for hours — the hall was 1,454 of 5,000 at best anyway. The chest is fed later and less.
- Measure: Treasuries "members stood" gp/h (3,500 before), members above the keep per guild, Money line median hourly; share under 100gp from `/api/state` bots[] every 10 min (dashboard's 6-minute `netPerBotPerHour` is too noisy to read).

**O2 — poor hunters hunt for gold (`BotQuarry.Paying`, `Barren`, `ZonePays`; `PayFirst` true, `PayReach` 2, `PayKnown` 3, `ZoneLeast` 0.5, `ZoneMost` 2.0).**
- `BotQuarry` already measured gold per kind (`Pays`, fed at every corpse; the city's head prices are added through `Rewarded`). A hunter under `BotHunter.PoorBelow` (100gp) whose ordinary look (Reach 50) found nothing or a kind killed `PayKnown` times for nothing looks twice as far for the best quarry that is not such a kind; the wider look runs only then (the loop is hot). In the zone choice a poor hunter's zone score is multiplied by what the zone's kinds have paid, 0.5 for a field of grazers up to 2.0 for a camp that pays — one line in `BotHunter.Hunting`, kept apart from zones5's fit work; `BotZones` untouched.
- Counters (Trade line, `BotQuarry.Describe`): "a poor hunter looks 2 times as far first for a kind that pays: N found one, M of a kind known to carry nothing passed over in that look, K zone looks weighed by what their kinds pay".
- Risk: harder quarry, more deaths among the poor (`Daring` 1.0, the breaker and the toll stand against it); a kind priced from one lucky corpse. Measure: solo corpse gp per hunt (19.5 on 388), kills with gold, deaths/bot-h of bots under 100gp, coin/bot-h of the poor.

**O3 — half the mint to prices on heads (`BotCity.HeadShare` 0.5, `HeadCap` 10,000, `HeadLeast`/`HeadMost` 20/60 at strength/`HeadPerPower` 25, `HeadEveryMs` 10 min, `HeadKills` 2, `MostKinds` 6, `HeadHourCap` 300).**
- Each mint tick puts half into a heads' purse (the treasury, fairs and lots get the other half; the mint's total is unchanged, what the heads' purse cannot hold goes to the treasury). Every ten minutes the kinds that killed at least two bots inside two hours (`BotKept.Fell` → `BotCity.Fell`; bots, pets and summons are not kinds) carry a price by their strength; a price lapses two hours after the last kill of ours. Paid at the corpse: a lone hunter's `BotSlay` and a company's `BotSpoils.Share` call `BotCity.Collect`, the price split equally like the gold, no hand taking more than 300gp an hour (the farming guard). Persisted as store shape 2; a shape-1 save is read as before and the purse starts empty.
- Counters (City line): "prices on kinds: N posted and M lapsed, K heads paid for Ggp (C hands at their hour's 300gp, U the heads' purse could not pay), Pgp in the heads' purse of 10000 (50 % of the mint); bounties: 40gp a head on Orc (12 of ours fell to them, 5 heads paid)". Lines per posting, lapse and payout.
- Risk: the shops lose half the fairs' demand (sell-through was 100 % only because of fairs); a company that farms a priced kind — capped per hand per hour; the price makes a kind "pay" in `BotQuarry`, so poor hunters go for the kinds that kill bots (that is the point, and the toll prices the ground). Measure: heads paid gp/h and to whom (share to bots under 100gp), fairs gp/h, shop sales.

**O4 — consumables from the pile before the counter (`BotShopper.PileMs` 3 min, in `bot-shops.json` as `PileMs`); a caster's casts capped by the quarry's gold (`BotSlay.CastsByGold`, `CastFloor` 2); reclaim by worth (`BotUndertaker.Least` 20); the death toll (`BotYield.DeathTollShare` 1.0).**
- Pile: a consumable the glut reads as piled (`BotGlut.Glutted`, factor ≤ 0.34 — bandages at ×0.10 all day) is said aloud at the counter's price before any walk, and a carrier holding some brings it; only a bot holding at least one of the thing waits, three minutes, then walks; not for arrows (a fight wants them now). Counters in the "At death's door" line: "N asked the island for a piled consumable before any counter (M looks waited, K walked after nobody came)".
- Casts: a Caster (Mage, Sage) takes no quarry that does not pay for two casts (`BotQuarry.Dear`, Trade line) unless it is at its throat; in the fight, once the casts have spent what one of the kind pays (`BotProvision.CastCost`: the scroll or the herbs at the market's price), the quarry is left alive and shunned two minutes, the hunt ends Done with the reason (`BotSlay.Thrifted`, in The island line). A WarriorMage is Melee and finishes with its sword.
- Reclaim: a corpse is priced by what lies in it (coin, goods at the market's price); under 20gp it is let go at once, above it the walk claims worth/1.5 a minute instead of a flat 20, so a corpse holding 80gp and bandages wins the auction it used to lose. Money line: "reclaims: N corpses worth Ggp gone back for, P left for holding under 20gp, O left for the ground round them".
- Toll: a death charges the work that died the supplies the next door will ask for (`BotProvision.Bill`, read with the pack already on the corpse: bandages, bottles, reagents at the market's price; ammunition is bound and left out) on top of the pocket and the three minutes. Per place, through the ledger, so quarry on ground that kills loses the auction there. Money line: "N deaths charged the work that died Ggp of supplies left on the corpse (100 % of the bill)"; the died-ending line shows ", 48 toll".
- Risk: the toll also flows into `BotCommons.Corrected` for the kind — if "nothing was worth doing" climbs (270/h on 387) or hunts fall, set `DeathTollShare` 0.5; a mage with no quarry worth two casts idles — watch the Mage's coin/bot-h, which was the worst; reclaim walks into killing fields (7 of 40 died on 386; the ground check `BotQuad.Muscle` still stands).

**The traders' own ribs (`BotHaul.Gather`).** `BotMarket.Wanted(bot, kind) != null` was a refusal, and every trader that cooks keeps a want for raw ribs open — the island's main want — so every gathering of ribs for a buyer failed at once. The standing want is now topped up by what the orders need (`BotMarket.Ask` tops rather than overwrites, at the trader's learned price) and said again at its own size and price when the gathering ends (`StopAsking`). Counter in the Traders line: "N gatherings (M said over the trader's own standing want)". Expected: haul share 79.8 % → ~88 %; measure `failed at haul: ... could not say the want` (38 on 388 → 0) and the Traders line's gathered units.

**How to measure after the deploy (first two 5-minute summaries, then hourly):** Treasuries (stood gp/h, UnderKeep, members above 800), Money (median, deaths charged, reclaims), City (heads paid and to whom, heads' purse, fairs), Trade (`Dear`, PaidFirst/BarrenPassed, GatherOverOwn), The island (`Thrifted`), At death's door (Piled/PileWaited/PileWalked), Delving line (supplies could not pay). Acceptance from `poverty-388.md`: share under 100gp from 55 % toward 35 % by hour 6, median 80 → 250–350 for guild members, haul share ≥ 88 %, deaths/bot-h not above 388's 1.56.

Patch: `econ5.patch` = `diff -ruN -x obj -x bin base388/Projects econ5/Projects`, 18 files, no configuration touched; dry-run and build verified on a fresh copy of base388 (0 errors, 0 warnings, copy identical to econ5).

**02.10.2026 · build 389 (written by Fable) · Prime time: the island's floor by the hour, the critical posts never absent, and the population filled to 200 in a burst**
- *Patrick, 02.10 ~00:20:* "Add a prime time for the bots: say at night from 00 to 08 in the morning 100 % of the bots play, from 08 to 15 — 75 %, from 16 to 23 — 50 %. Let us populate the world up to 200 bots right away. Only make sure the world is never left without critically important bots. Make it an additional setting: this is done so that we collect as much data as possible at night and focus on the improvement work during the day." Taken as 00–08, 08–16 and 16–24, local server time.
- *Measured on 388 (`session-2026-10-02_00-14.log`) and the day before:* 90 bots on the island (80 of the mix + 10 newcomers), **55 in the world and 35 resting** at 00:20; by 09:16, nine hours into the same session, **100 bots (ten more newcomers at two every two hours), 53 in the world and 47 resting** — the night passed at just over half, which is what the order is against; through 01.10's 7.5 h run (`12-05.log`) 43–46 of 86 in the world at every reading, night and day alike — `BotRest.FloorShare` 0.5 round the clock and nothing that knows the hour. Neither `BotRest` nor `BotGrowth` had a configuration key (DIALS.md: *code only* for all seventeen). Loop cost: **4.01 ms a 100 ms look with 43–46 in the world** (1 019 396 ms over 253 925 looks on 12:05), 4.31–4.43 ms on 387's 23:14 run (45–47), 6.10 ms over 388's first five minutes with 55 (boot included); deciding **0.074 ms a turn** (429 513 ms over 5 822 860 turns), walking 0.093 ms a turn; 843 slow ticks (>100 ms) in 7.5 h ≈ 1.9 a minute, every one a single bot's proposer (Miner 250–562 ms, Shopper 121 ms) or the five-minute summary. About **0.085 ms per present bot per look.**
- *Why one number for both directions:* the floor already did both halves of the job on 388 — kept the ones past their hours playing while the island was under it, and brought the resting back when it fell under — so the prime time is the floor made a function of the hour rather than a second mechanism beside it. Rest and return follow the one target; nothing new pulls a bot out of anything: a bot the target lets go only tires and leaves by `BotRest.Holds`' rules (not from a fight, a company, a delve, a cell; let go of work or company after `GraceMs`).
- *Decision (`BotPrime`: `Running`, `RampMinutes` 30, `TirePerLook` 5, `ReturnPerLook` 5, `Bands` 00–08 1.0 / 08–16 0.75 / 16–24 0.5; config `PrimeTime` in the new `bot-rest.json`):* `BotRest.Look` reads `BotPrime.Share(now)` where it read `FloorShare`; the floor in bots is `ceil(share × island)` (resting counted), the allowance to tire is `present − onCall − floor − tiredAlready` as before. **Ramp:** for `RampMinutes` after a band begins the share moves linearly from the band before (round the clock at midnight) to the band's own, so 200 at 100 % become 150 at 75 % at about 1.7 a minute over 08:00–08:30 rather than fifty in one look, and the night fills 00:00–00:30 at about 3 a minute. **Caps behind the ramp:** at most `TirePerLook` tired and `ReturnPerLook` brought back in one look (every 20 s); neither binds while the ramp runs, both would if the schedule were edited to a jump. **Return:** with the schedule on, the window for coming back under the floor is the whole rest (388's `EarlyMinutes` 60 only when it is off), soonest due first; a bot back this way is counted `BotPrime.Returned` and said "prime time (00–08 at 100 %, ramping) wants 200 of the island's 200 in the world and it had 148"; one within 60 minutes of its time still counts as 388's `Early`. Off, every number is 388's. Overlapping or malformed bands are dropped by name at the load; with none valid, the three written stand; an hour no band holds falls to `FloorShare`.
- *Decision (`BotCritical`: `Running`, `EarlyMinutes` 480, `Floors` Healer 3, Crafter 4, Gatherer 4, Mage 3, Trader 3, Captain 1, Baron 1, Smith 1, Tailor 1, Fletcher 1, Miner 1, Woodsman 1; config `Critical` in `bot-rest.json`, the `Floors` table replaced whole when named):* a post is a class by name or a trade a producer holds **by its best skill** — Blacksmith/Tailoring/Fletching among crafters, Mining/Lumberjacking among gatherers, ties to the first listed, so a crafter born even is a smith; every bot fills its class's post and a producer one trade's besides. Three gates in the rest clock: (1) **hold** — in the `_due` loop, after the island's floor and the traders' share, a bot whose post has `present ≤ floor` (in the world and not tired, counted once a look before anybody is tired and kept current through `Tired`/`Back`/`Born`) plays on, counted `_heldCritical` and `BotCritical.Held`, said once per spell ("is past its hours but plays on: the island would be under its 1 Baron(s) without it"); (2) **return** — after the island's own returns, each post short of its floor brings its own back from rest, soonest due first, up to `EarlyMinutes` (eight hours: the whole of any rest) early, as many as it is short, counted `Brought` — this is what fills the gap a restart leaves (bots resting at the save stay away through `Reclaim`) or a death; (3) **birth** — `BotGrowth.Pick` asks `BotCritical.Wanting` first: a post with fewer on the whole island (resting counted) than its floor gets the next newcomer in its **class** (a trade asks for its class; which trade a crafter leans to is drawn by its name in `BotBirth`, so it cannot be ordered), counted `ByPost`. The Baron, one of one with a floor of one, never tires: Patrick's "never left without". The traders' share rule of 388 stands beside the Trader floor.
- *Decision (`BotGrowth.FillTo` 200, `BurstBy` 5, `Most` stays 210; config `Growth` in `bot-population.json`, which also reaches `Running`, `EveryMinutes`, `By`, `Most`, `LeastToWant` for the first time):* while the island (world + away) is under `min(FillTo, Most)`, every look of the rest clock raises up to `BurstBy` newcomers through the same `Pick`/`RaiseNewcomer` as the two-hourly growth — the mix's proportions among classes with more than one (the Baron excluded; Captains, Architects, Sages and Brawlers at 2 of 79 each as the growth already draws them), `BotBirth`'s leanings, a fresh name of a people (Human 80 names × 23 houses, Elf and Dwarf 60 × 11 — ample), `Enlist`'s first turn spread over `BotWill.IdleMs` (build 382) — written into `_added` so `Reclaim` keeps them at the next boot, and put somewhere into its first session by `BotRest.Spread` (`FirstShare` 0.85, as the ones met at a boot are) so 110 born in seven minutes do not tire inside the same few hours. The guild-gap rule (`LeastToWant`) is skipped in the burst — a hundred draws would answer one guild's want many times over before the first had joined anybody — and the two-hour clock runs on beside it. One line a look ("The burst: 5 newcomers (…); the island now has 105 bots towards 200") and one when it is done. **From the 100 on the island at 09:16, 100 newcomers in 20 looks ≈ 7 minutes; the ceiling is 210, the fill 200**, so the slow growth keeps two every two hours above it. Deployed in the 08–16 band (75 %, the ramp long over at 09:16), the target is 150 of 200: the hundred newcomers arrive in the world and are not sent to rest for it — the floor only ever keeps bots on — and the ones past their hours already there go as they come free, at most five a look. A new world after a wipe raises the mix at the boot and then fills to 200 the same way.
- *Loop cost at 200, from the measured 0.085 ms per present bot per look:* 200 in the world (the night's target) ≈ **17 ms a 100 ms look, 17 % of one core**; deciding ≈ 1000 turns/s × 0.074 ms ≈ 74 ms/s; 150 by day ≈ 13 ms, 100 by evening ≈ 8.5 ms. The worst ticks stay single-bot (one Miner proposer at 560 ms is 560 ms whoever else is there) and come about 4× as often, ≈ 8 a minute. The boot is unchanged in kind: `Reclaim` takes 200 back where it took 90, and 382's spread puts their first turns over twenty ticks. A burst look costs five births (Become, outfit, placement) on top of a look, once per 20 s for seven minutes, inside the slow-tick budget. `BotRest.Look` and `BotCritical.Count` are a pass over 200 and a few skill reads, nothing against a look.
- *Counted:* the `Rest:` line now reads "… in the world, … resting (…); prime time: band 00–08 at 100 % (ramping from 50 % with 12 of 30 minutes in), target 100 % = 200 of 200 in the world against 148 there (52 short); bands 00–08 at 100 %, 08–16 at 75 %, 16–24 at 50 %, the target moving over 30 minutes at a band's start; this session N brought back by it (up to 5 a look, N looks held more), N tires put off by the pace of 5 a look; N past their hours and playing on so the island is not left under its floor of 200 (N traders …, N for a critical post, N put off a look by the pace); critical floors: Healer 7/3, Crafter 9/4, …, Tailor 0/1 (none on the island), … — 11 of 12 held; this session N times a bot past its hours was kept in the world for a post, N brought back from rest for one (up to 480 minutes early), N newcomers born into a post the island lacked; …" and the growth clause "newcomers: 2 every 120 minutes up to 210 bots (the burst filling to 200 at 5 a look, 110 to go, N raised by it this session)". The boot line "Prime time ON: 00–08 at 100 %, 08–16 at 75 %, 16–24 at 50 % of the island in the world, local time, … critical floors ON: Healer 3, …" is the proof of the live values. `DIALS.md` regenerated: `BotRest` ×13, `BotPrime` ×4, `BotCritical` ×2 and `BotGrowth` ×7 now reachable.
- *Watch:* `Rest:` "target … against … there": at night the gap closes within the ramp and stays at nought; by day 150 ± the ramp; "none short" most readings. "The clock: … ms a look" ≤ 20 at 200 present; slow ticks a minute ≤ 10. "The burst:" lines at 5 a look to 200 and "The burst is done" within ten minutes of the deploy; `Guilds:` "belong to none" falling to nought within fifteen (`Gather` seats one every 5 s). "critical floors … held" 12 of 12 at every reading, or a named post with "(none on the island)" and a newcomer "born a Crafter: the island has 0 of its 1 Tailor(s)" after it. At 08:00–08:30 the tired lines come at about two a minute, not fifty in a look.
- *Risk:* the night's target is the whole island, so "past their hours and playing on" will read in the dozens all night — honest, and the price of the order. Bots brought back by the schedule start a fresh session (as any return does), so a bot pulled back at 00:05 after an hour's rest plays the night through and is among the first to go at 08:00. The 08:00 ramp sends about fifty to bed over thirty minutes, each leaving as it comes free — a visible wave, bounded. A trade's floor can stand unfilled for a while when no crafter's best skill is the trade (with Tailor at 1 of 10 weight, 21 % of fifteen crafters have none): the line names it and the next newcomer is a Crafter whose leaning the name decides, so it is filled by chance rather than by order. A post's floor counts dead bots as present (the reviver's business) and never cuts a rest for a bot on a war call (the away never are). 110 newcomers raise the guild count (anyone may found) and so the expansion and the war risk Patrick accepted on 26.09; the muster will show it. Loop figures above are a linear projection from 45–55 present and should be read against the first hour's "The clock:" line.

**01.10.2026 · build 388 (written by Fable) · The road is priced for the one who walks it, and a node no walk reaches is refused, not priced**
- *Patrick (night plan v2, point 5):* "bots know where to hunt, what is nearer, where there are more mobs, and how to go round areas, with a margin or without, to pass without trouble." *Point 6:* "refusal zones never have route points built onto them, saving precious time."
- *Measured on 386 (Opus dossier, rows 1 and 8; 701 deaths, 2.10 a bot-hour):* 71 % of deaths inside a deadly zone; 124 of 139 prowl deaths more than a hundred tiles from the prowl's target; Trinsic's 17 residents 52 % of all deaths. *On 387's first 23 minutes (23:14–23:37, `roads4-tools/deaths387-first.txt`):* 66 deaths, 47 of them solo, and in 36 of the 47 the bot's strength was under a quarter of its killer's — bots are not losing fights they chose; they are met on the road by things four times their size. 17 of the 66 near Trinsic, 13 near Yew, 12 near Britain, 11 near Cove.
- *Why:* `BotDanger.Cost` priced every node against the median bot (`BotZone.VsBot`, reference 1116): the same +300 tiles of detour for a novice alone and for a company of eight, so a company went round ground it could have crossed and a novice crossed ground that was priced as if it were the median. And the planners knew nothing of the reach map: a node on a roof, in a sealed yard or on an isle was a node like any other, expanded and relaxed.
- *Calibration (live zones at 23:37, `roads4-tools/zones_now.json`):* zone 28 "reapers and whipping vines, W of Trinsic" is 1223 × 1919 tiles, fight 22,935 (×20.6 the reference, 12 can close at once); zone 27 "reapers and gargoyles, NE of Britain" 30,462 (×27), 867 × 579 tiles; zone 17 east of Yew 47,945 (×43). The straight road from Trinsic's bank to Britain's lies in zone 28's paint for about a thousand tiles; Yew to Britain crosses zones 17, 5, 18 and 27. Trinsic's bank itself falls inside zone 28's smoothed outline (the dashboard's 64-point rings; the raster the code reads is finer), so no verdict on a road may be taken from a zone the walker already stands in.
- *Decision (`BotDanger.For`/`Clear`, `BotWalk` round `BotJourney.Leg`; `ByWalker` switch):* the walk names the walker before a route is drawn, and the hook prices each node against that walker's strength — its company's when it is in one (`BotQuad.Strength`). A patrol zone's fight divided by that strength takes the place of `VsBot`: the fringe costs `EdgePerBot` a time, a hostile patrol `HostilePerBot` a time between `HostileLeast` and `HostileMost`, and a deadly zone costs `DeadlyCost` only while its fight is `DeadlyVsWalker` (3) times the walker or more — below that it is charged the hostile price, and the company cuts through. A bloodied square whose record asks more than `RoadDare` (1.5) times the walker costs `BloodBeyond` (300) rather than `BloodCost` (60). Routes drawn without a walker (the travel book, a delve's seat-to-gate, the door) are priced for the median bot as before. Bounded: no node costs more than `BarredCost` (800) tiles, as the overflow of 29.09 demands.
- *Decision (`RefusesNodes`):* for a walker on open ground, a node the reach map calls anything but open — and for one aboard a ship, anything but water — answers `NavCost.Unaffordable`, which the planners' `Relax` declines, so no route point is built on refused ground and no search expands into it. Measured on the hook's own counter.
- *Decision (`NavRouteMemory.Round`, the one engine line):* a remembered detour is served while it is no bloodier than when it was drawn and still quieter than the ground road *for whoever asks now*. The old rule asked that the ground road be no quieter than when the detour was drawn, which, with a hook that answers differently for a company and for a bot alone, dropped and redrew the same detour at every change of walker (a plan is 5.7 ms on average on 387 and 2.5 s at worst).
- *Counted, in `Getting about:` (`BotDanger.Describe`):* "N routes priced for the walker that asked (on), N nodes refused outright on ground the reach map says the walker cannot reach (on)"; "N bloodied (… N of them +300 for a record past the walker's strength ×1.5)"; "N deadly (+300; N of them at the hostile price for a walker the fight did not reach ×3)". Dials in `bot-movement.json`: `DangerByWalker`, `DeadlyVsWalker`, `BloodBeyond`, `RefuseNodes`.
- *Watch:* `paths.share` on `/api/state` at or above 0.99 (0.9957 at 23:37 on 387); `routes.overBudget` and `routes.unreachable` (6 and 95 of 1840 at 23:37) — a goal whose own graph node lies on refused ground now fails the planner and falls to the chart; "detoured" against "throughBlood" (260 : 190) and `RoundFallbacks`; the worst route ms.

The zone's fight is the strongest of the zone with what can close at once — one number for a zone of 2 million tiles — so the pricing is coarse where the zone is; the record of deaths (`BotQuad`) is what refines it.

"{kind} is over a road that asks N of strength at (x, y) by the record of what has killed there / the patrol of zone Z, against the M it brings".

  - `BotShops.Nearest`: a counter over such a road is passed over for the next one the buyer can reach alive, so the restock is still offered (`DeadlyRoad`, in the shops' line).
  - `BotGround` seams: a seam over such a road is passed over by the same odds as `MineOdds` (`RoadOutmuscled`, in the ground line).

A company of four (≈4,800) refuses samples over 7,200: zones 5, 18 and 52 are open to it, 27, 28, 17 and 45 are not. A Trinsic resident bound for Britain stands in zone 28 and ends in zone 27, so for it only the record of deaths on the way counts — and on 387 the squares at (1800, 3000) and (1800, 3100) already hold seven. The expected saving is honest and small for the searches — water and rock were never walkable by the step mask, so what pruning removes is standing ground reachable only by a one-way drop (ledges, roofs, isles) — and larger for the planners, whose nodes the graph joined across item walls the map knows of.

**01.10.2026 · build 388 (written by Fable) · A band's company comes up to its quarry together and engages when it is there; a company without a medic levies the nearest healer**
- *Patrick, 01.10:* companies 99 %; maximum responsiveness; "support for the dying with healing and magic"; members answer the company's focus within a beat or two.
- *Measured on 387 (`session-2026-10-01_19-33.log`, 19:33–20:38, 65 min, ~44 bots):* first blows on a band's quarry came a mean of **25.1 s** after the company engaged (101 blows over 44 fights; 7 inside 2 s, 79 past 10 s; 44 members never had one: 24 blades, 9 shooters, 11 back ranks), against **8.9 s** for a prowl's company (107 over 67) and 6.3 s for a restock's. In the 23:14 run (15 min): band 15.4 s, prowl 5.2 s. Help for the hurt after build 387's `BindSkill` 20: 95 fell under half, **47 helped (49.5 %, was 13.3 % on 386)**, 26 died unhelped (27.4 %, was 41.9 %), 36 heals aimed at the dying, 0 by mages; 23:14 run: 30 of 57 helped (52.6 %), 12 unhelped (21 %). So the bind fix did most of what row 5 asked; what is left is the levy without a medic (43 % of companies on 386) and the band's slow first blow.
- *Why the band is slow:* `BotBand.Calling` levied the nearest free bots within `BotMuster.Reach` (120 tiles) and called `Engage` in the same beat. The first-blow clock starts at the engagement; the members were still 30–120 tiles off, walking to stations round the quarry one by one, and the first blows came one by one — which is also how bands of three to five fought their quarry two at a time and died on 386. A prowl's company walks to its ground already gathered and engages what it finds, hence 5–9 s.
- *Decision (`BotBand.Gathers` switch, `Gathering` stage; `EngageTiles` 10, `GatherTiles` 12, `GatherMs` 30 s; config `BandGathers`, `BandEngageTiles`, `BandGatherTiles`, `BandGatherMs` in `bot-hunt.json`):* after the levy the band does not engage. The squad is charged (`Charged`, so it does not age), put on the march (`OnTheMarch`, so the leader is paced to the members behind it by `BotSquad.Lagging` exactly as a delve's or a prowl's column is, and nobody is scattered), and its own finder is stilled (`Quarry = Nothing`). The leader walks up to `EngageTiles` of the quarry (`BotDoing.Walk` following the creature) with the column behind it, then stands until every living member is within `GatherTiles` of it or `GatherMs` is up, and engages then — with everybody in reach of the first beat. Set upon on the way, the company engages at once (`BotSquads.Note` sets the focus; the band's `Fighting` already treats the company's fight as its own and turns back to the quarry after). The quarry gone before the company comes up ends the band finished (as `Fighting` ends it on the quarry's death); moved off past `BotMuster.Reach` ends it failed and the company disbanded (as the short levy does). The charge, the march and the finder are given back at the engagement and at `Drop`.
- *Decision (`BotBand.LevyMedic`, `MedicReach` 150, `Medics` switch; config `BandMedicReach`):* a company that holds no member of role `Medic` (`BotFormation.RoleOf`; mages are not medics, their heals wait on reagents — 0 heals by mages at the dying on 387) levies the nearest free healer within `MedicReach` after the fighters and before the company is judged. Asked by the band's call and by the prowl's company (`BotProwl`, the same levy loop). The healer is pressed to the enlistment like every other member and walks up with the column.
- *Counted:* in `Companies:` → bands clause: "N companies walked up to their quarry before engaging (on): N engaged with everybody within 12 tiles of the leader, N on the 30s clock with members still behind, N set upon on the way, N found the quarry gone and N gone off past 120 tiles; N medics levied into a company that had none and N companies that found no free healer within 150 tiles". The first-blow instrument ("band N over N fights (a mean of Ns …)") is the measure.
- *Watch:* band mean first blow (25.1 s → ≤ 8 s); band "never had one" (44 of 145 slots → ≤ 20 %); bands finished (42.9 % on 387's first half hour, 56 % over 65 min → ≥ 60 %); company deaths in band work; "members fell under 50 % … helped" (49.5 % → ≥ 60 %) and "died unhelped" (27 % → ≤ 20 %); `MedicsWanting` against `MedicsLevied` (a high wanting count says the healers are all resting or at work the levy will not cost them).
- *Risk:* a leader standing ten tiles from an aggressive quarry for up to thirty seconds is set upon before the column is up (counted `SetUpon`); that is the old behaviour at worst, with the members nearer. The walk-up costs the band up to a minute before its fight; the quarry may wander (`MovedOff`). A healer levied from 150 tiles is the slowest member and may arrive after the fight; the gather waits for it only up to `GatherMs`.

- *Decision (`BotTrading.RestShare` 0.5, `RestEarlyMinutes` 180, `BotTrading.Trader`; `BotRest.Traders`; config `RestShare`, `RestEarlyMinutes` in `bot-traders.json`):* in the look that sends tired bots to rest, a trader past its hours is kept playing on while the traders resting or already tired are at `floor(RestShare × all traders)` — three of seven — exactly as the island's floor keeps bots on; and when more than that share are away (a restart that found four of seven resting, as 23:14 did), the trader due back soonest within `RestEarlyMinutes` is brought back early, one a look. Counted `PutAways`, `PutAwayGold`. Nought keeps everything in the pocket, as before. No gold is created: the pocket is moved, not topped up.
- *Counted:* in `Traders:` → "capital: N times a trader put Ngp in all into its account above a pocket float of 100gp; rest: N traders past their hours kept in the world so no more than 50 % of the traders rest at once, N brought back early for it"; and in `Rest:` → "(N traders so no more than 50 % of the traders rest at once)".

**01.10.2026 · build 387 (written by Fable) · Hunters hit monsters: a quarry of the grazing kind at hand is passed over for a zone's fighter within the walk**
- *Patrick, 01.10:* hunters hit monsters, not cows; the aggressive first; harmless monsters and animals second, and only when no aggressive one is within reach of the walk.
- *Measured on 386 (12:06–18:34, 329 bot-hours, `hunt-delve-386.txt`):* hunters were sent after 94 creatures at their throat, 476 that fight whoever comes near and 3231 of the grazing kind (85 %); of 689 solo kills 266 (38.6 %) were livestock, deer and pets at 0 gp and 209 (30.3 %) wild beasts at 60 gp between them; 125 gp a bot-hour; 43.8 % of prowls ended "nothing here". The zones were named as ground 16648 times and chosen 1971, and 32 of those arrived to find nothing — the zone path works when it is taken.
- *Why:* `BotQuarry.Best` ranks what is hostile first (build 385), but only among what stands within thirty tiles of the hunter, and round a town that is the cows, sheep, boars and great harts of the fields; the zones (`BotHunter.Zoned`, the fifth named ground) were consulted only when nothing at all stood within thirty tiles. A grazer at hand always won over a fighter three hundred tiles off. The Opus dossier (19:02) adds the other half: 1,228,731 creature looks were passed over by Best as "on ground asking more strength than it brought" — the monsters by the towns stand in deadly squares, the cows do not.
- *Decision (`BotHunter.Propose`, `GrazersLast` switch; `Hunting`/`Zoned` give back the zone's creature):* when the quarry at hand is of the grazing kind — not at this bot's throat, and not of a kind that fights whoever comes near (`BotQuarry.Fights`, bears, wolves and cougars included, which the engine makes `FightMode.Aggressor`) — the hunter asks its named grounds; when the ground that wins is a hostile zone's living fighter it could take alone (`ZoneDare`, `Daring`, the ground's own tests), that fighter is its quarry: claimed and walked to as a `BotSlay`, priced by the auction as the hunt it is, not as a prowl at 8. When the fighter's ground asks a company the bots standing by can make (`BotQuad.Together`), the company prowl is raised instead (the existing mechanism, `CompanyTookOn`). Only when neither is to be had does the grazer stay. The board's own creature (`BotCharter.Carved`, hides) still outranks the zone, as it has since 15.09.
- *Decision (`BotQuarry.Best`, `FightsBack`):* within the choice at hand, what fights back when struck (the engine's `FightMode.Aggressor`: bears, wolves, cougars, boars, harts) ranks above what fights nothing (`FightMode.None`: cows, sheep, pigs, horses) — the Sonnet analyst's reading of "the aggressive first, the harmless second": a wolf ranked with a cow because `Fights` is false for both.
- *Decision (`BotHunter.Zoned`, `ZoneCompanies` switch):* a hostile zone too strong for the hunter alone is no longer dropped before the ground's tests can ask for a company; it is weighed against what the bots standing by would bring together (`BotThreat.OurPower` within `BotMuster.Reach`, as the band's call weighs its quarry), and `Hunting`'s own tests — the zone's fight against the hunter alone, the quadrant's muscle, the peril map, `BotQuad.Together` at the gate — make it a company prowl or pass it over. Sonnet: of 188 hostile zones only 29 suited a lone bot; companies took 97 gp a bot-hour against a lone hunt's 12.
- *Counted:* "N quarry of the grazing kind at hand passed over for a zone's fighter within the walk and N for a company raised against one whose ground asked it (grazers last)" and "N hostile zones kept as ground for a company, too strong for the hunter alone" in `The island:`; the three "hunters sent after … at their throat / that fight / of the grazing kind (N of them of a kind that fights back when struck)" in `Trade:` are the measure.
- *Watch:* the grazing share of "hunters sent after" (85 % on 386; the dossier's bar is ≤ 30 %); passive share of solo kills (38.6 %); gold a bot-hour (125); "could not catch" and "drew it N tiles" (a far quarry may cost those); prowls "nothing here".
- *Risk:* a hunter that cannot reach the zone's creature (a pocket Best's `ShutOff` did not see from afar) ends "could not catch" after `BotSlay.CapMs` (150 s) and crowds it for two minutes; the hunter walks further for its kills, so deaths on the road (dossier row 1, reach3's `BotDanger`) weigh more on hunting.

**01.10.2026 · build 387 (written by Fable) · Three fruitless swings are three swings of the engine's slowest weapon, not of a four-second one**
- *Measured on 386:* companies broke off "its health has not moved" 434 times against 883 "it is down"; 82 of them with one of two able to strike, 56 with two of two, 41 with one of three, 39 with one of one; mostly from ettins (33), trolls (28), harpies (27), ogres (24), whipping vines, reapers and grizzly bears. Bands: 70 finished of 261 (26.8 %), "broke off — health has not moved" 53, died 52, "never got near it" 43.
- *Why:* `BotSquad.SlowestBlowMs` (4000) was read off a formula that is not the engine's. `BaseWeapon.GetDelay` on this era is floor(80000 / ((Stam + 100) × speed) − 2) quarter-second ticks: at the bots' sixty stamina a crossbow swings every 6.25 s, a bow every 4.5, a longsword every 3.5, and slower as the stamina goes. Three "blows" of four seconds gave a bow two shots and a crossbow one; a company of two at 40–60 % to hit then misses the whole window one time in four or five, and every break-off shuns the creature for fifteen minutes (`HopelessMs`) and hands the next hunter "would not go down".
- *Decision (`BotSquad.SlowestBlowMs` 6000; `Blows` stays 3):* eighteen seconds — three swings of the slowest weapon in the kit, as the number says it means. No config sets either.
- *Measured by Sonnet, the other half:* bands and small companies are justified by a crowd that never joins — the call weighs the quarry against everybody able within 120 tiles × `Tolerance` (1.5), the levy takes whoever is free and not at work the enlistment would cost it, a median of three: companies of two or three put their quarry down 52 %, of five or six 85 %; 52 bands died; ogres 3 of 39, whipping vines 0 of 22, reapers 1 of 15.
- *Decision (`BotBand.Calling`, `Rejudged` switch, `Brought`):* the company that came is judged against the same bar before it engages — its members' strength × `Tolerance` against what the fight asks (`Asked`: the quarry and what menaces round it) — and a company short of it does not engage: "only N came against X: S of strength to the A it asks", the quarry left alone for `ShunMs` (two minutes) so the same few do not call the same short company on the next beat, the members let go to their work.
- *Counted:* "N not engaged because the company that came fell short of the fight (judged after the levy)" in the bands clause of `Companies:`.
- *Watch:* "broke off … its health has not moved" against "it is down" (434 : 883 on 386); the band's finish share (26.8 %) and "only N came against" among its failures (a band not engaged is a failure that costs a beat, not five bots); company deaths in band work (52); the kill rate (4.76 a bot-hour), which is the number that says whether the longer window cost anything, as the note on `Blows` warns.
- *Risk:* fewer bands engage, so fewer company kills until the levy brings enough — the gold a bot-hour from corpses divided (97) is the number to read beside the deaths.
- *Not changed:* "never got near it" 43 — companies that did not close on quarry found up to 120 tiles off (`BotMuster.Reach`) for 30 s; the clock is torn up while anybody closes, so these are walks that stopped. The road's business (reach3).

- *Measured:* 38,174 pass-overs "wanted by the trader itself" (a counter per want per look). Every trader cooks, so every trader keeps a standing want for raw ribs — the board's largest want, 46 % of all units asked for on 384, 297 units for 4,908gp handed hand to hand on 386 — and that want shut the whole kind to the trader: ribs were hauled nine times.

**01.10.2026 · build 387 (written by Fable) · Cloth at two against bandages at five, with the road priced**
- *Opus dossier row 4, measured:* 336 restock errands "after N Cloth", **76 died (24 %, 11 % of every death on the shard)**, 1,767 bot-minutes. They set out from Trinsic, Yew and Minoc and ended at Phyllis in Britain (104 of the cloth buys), while `Balance:` read Bandage 106–158 and Cloth 150 piled against 0 asked.

And `BotShops.Nearest` passed a counter across the water: 12 errands "no way through to Tamma in Serpent's Hold", 2 each to Delucia and Moonglow.

The weavers' pile is reached by the shops when fighters' wants stand (`BotShopkeep.Demanded` reads open wants).
- *Watch:* restock "after N Cloth" deaths ≤ 3 % of its endings; `ClothFarther` > 0 from Trinsic; "no way through to Tamma" at nought; Bandage and Cloth off the glut list within two hours.
- *Code:* `BotShops/BotShopper.cs`, `BotShops/BotShops.cs`.
