**01.10.2026 · build 387 (written by Fable, wave 3) · Bots answer each other's moods: a tag behind every mood line, and help offered through the auction**

**Patrick's words** (night plan v2, point 4, in English): "Bots actively talk to each other, they read each other's mood
from the phrases, and depending on the mood other bots offer company or help. Not across hostile guilds. Give this to
Fable to implement and review."

**Measured, build 386 (12:05–18:37, about 86 bots).**
- 1,323 mood lines in six and a half hours, about 2.4 per online bot-hour (the clock is one in fifteen minutes; rest and
  the inn take the remainder). Over the whole day 4,704 mood lines: 79 % were the four "high" lines ("Good day for it",
  "Never felt better" …), 17 % "mid", 4 % "low". A mood was one number (contentment) in three bands, and nothing in it
  said *what* was wrong — "My purse is empty and so is my patience" came up for a bot that was merely bored.
- Every one of them was said wherever the bot stood. At 18:40 the state read 43 living bots, 20 of them with nobody
  within twelve tiles and 23 with somebody (4 with one neighbour, 9 with two, 8 with three, 2 with four or more); 54
  ordered pairs within earshot, 16 of the same guild, 26 with a guildless side. So about half the moods were said to the
  log, and the half said to somebody was answered by nobody, because nothing listened.
- The road chat (`BotMeetings`) looks at three tiles: 14,441 looks, 14,399 with nobody within three (99.7 %), 13 stops
  in six hours. The camp's fires carried 346 lines. Both are company by chance, not an answer to anything said.
- The help already exists and answers nothing said: the surgeon offers the worst-hurt within twenty tiles by ability,
  the camper lights a fire for its own tiredness, the muster calls a band for big quarry, the enlister joins fighting
  companies. None of them is triggered by a neighbour's words, and none is counted as an answer.

**Why this shape.**
- *Mood is legible.* `BotMoods.Read` gives every mood line one tag, worst first — `hurt`, `tired`, `grieving`, `poor`,
  `lonely`, `bored`, `proud`, else `content`/`middling`/`glum` from the old contentment scale — each read off a fact the
  shard keeps: the mender's own `Wants`, the rest's weariness (`BotCamp.Weariness`), the hunter's own poverty line
  (`BotHunter.PoorBelow`, one line for the shard rather than a second number on the same shelf) or the urges' need, the
  urges' boredom and barrenness, and two small records fed from the death and ending hooks the voice already has (grief
  for twenty minutes after a death in the guild, pride for ten after work that paid forty a minute). *Bored* and *lonely*
  are given only to a bot with nothing in hand or on a guess: boredom holds while a bot works and falls only when it is
  paid, so a miner two minutes into a seam still carries the wait before it, and "bored" said at a seam would be answered
  with a company's call that takes the bot off the seam. The tag rides behind the words — `data: {"mood":"poor"}` on the
  event stream, ` #poor` at the end of the speech-log line — and the seven new phrase keys (`mood:poor` …) say which mood
  in words, so the person at the log reads it as the bot in earshot does.
- *Listeners read what was said.* The voice raises `BotVoice.MoodSaid(speaker, tag, line, audience)`; `BotSocial.Heard`
  answers the tag and never asks the speaker how it feels. The deed that carries the help out checks the world itself,
  because that is the deed's business: a bandage is wound only on a wound (`BotSalve`), a fire only where one may be laid.
- *A mood is said to somebody.* A mood line due with nobody within `BotVoice.Earshot` (12) now waits, looking again every
  minute for up to ten (`MoodHoldMs`), then is said anyway. This changes only *when* a line is said — the voice's one
  invariant, that it never changes what the population does, holds — and it is what makes "I am broke" reach a neighbour
  who can answer it. One spatial query per due line is the whole cost, and the social layer reuses that query's list
  rather than making its own.
- *Words at once, help through the auction.* The nearest `MostListeners` (2) not of a hostile guild (`BotRegard.Hostile`,
  either way) and welcome by the engine's own notoriety (`BotCamp.Welcome`, so a red or a criminal is passed over) each
  answer once in `AnswerEveryMs` (2 min) and a pair once in `PairEveryMs` (20 min): a line for the mood three seconds later,
  thanks back half the time. Where the listener can also *do* something, the deed is written against it as an invitation
  and handed to its own auction by `BotFellow` at its next review — `BotSalve` for the hurt, `BotKindle` beside the tired
  (and the lonely) when it is a fire-lighter on wild ground with the means, `BotBand` on the biggest thing within the
  hunter's reach for the poor and the bored ("hunt together": the band's own call takes the speaker, who is nearest), and
  `BotEnlist` into the speaker's company for the lonely. The auction weighs it against what the listener holds: a seam at
  sixty a minute keeps the bot against a bandage at thirty, an idle bot goes. That is the whole of "it must not pull bots
  off paying work at a bad moment". The offer's own line ("Hold still, I have bandages") is said only when the offer is
  taken up (from `BotWill.Started`), never at the invitation, so no bot promises what its auction then refuses. An offer
  not taken in `InviteMs` (90 s) lapses; one whose speaker has gone, or — for a bandage — has been mended by somebody
  else, is let go; both are counted.
- *One answer is not an auction, and it is the company's own.* A listener already in a company asks a lonely or bored
  speaker in through the door every company has used since 01.10.2026 (`BotSquads.Enrol`), which takes only a bot whose
  work resumes; the layer adds that the speaker must be on nothing, a guess or unpaid work. The enlister the other way
  round (listener free, speaker in a company) is an ordinary offer.
- *No handouts.* A poor bot is answered with a hunt or with "coin comes to those who hunt"; nothing is given.
- *Cheap.* Hearing is a loop over the audience list of one mood line (a few per minute shard-wide); the proposer is a
  dictionary read per review; the replies are a list walked once a second; the pair and listener clocks are swept once
  a minute like the meetings'. No pass over the population, no O(n²).

**Decision.** New folder `BotSocial/`: `BotSocial` (hearing, answers, invitations, the counters), `BotFellow`
(`IBotProposer` on the Free rung), `BotSocialTalk` (the words: `fellow:*`, `offer:*`, `answer:thanks`, put into the
voice's bank only where the bank has nothing), `BotSocialModule` ("Social", world phase, after Population, Will and
Voice; `Configuration/bot-social.json`, PascalCase, a starter written with the code's values; a one-second timer).
In `BotVoice/`: `BotMoods` (the tag and its two records), `BotVoice.Earshot`/`MoodHoldMs`/`MoodRetryMs` in
`bot-voice.json`, `BotVoice.MoodSaid`, `Say(..., tag)` writing the tag to the event's `data` and the log, `Died` and
`Ended` feeding grief and pride, seven `mood:*` keys in `BotPhrases`. `BotCore` registers the module after the voice;
`BotBeat` writes `Society:` after `Camp:`; `Voice:` (the module's `Describe`) now also says moods said to somebody,
to nobody, and waits. MAP.md and regen-map.py carry the folder.

**Watch** (`Society:` every five minutes, cumulative per session; `Voice:` beside it).
- The share of moods said to somebody: on 386 about half; expect well over three quarters with the wait, at no more
  mood lines per bot-hour than before (the clock is unchanged at fifteen minutes). If `waits for an audience` grows
  without `said to somebody` growing, bots are alone for longer than ten minutes and the hold is doing nothing.
- The mood distribution after the wipe: everybody is poor, so `poor` will dominate and the hunt offers with it. Watch
  `offers: hunt N` against `finished (hunt n)` and the band's own "nobody was free to come": a band on the nearest
  mongbat is two bots on a rat, which the ledger corrects but the finished share still counts. If hunt offers fail
  more than they finish, lower `OffersHunts` to words (`false`) and let the poor bot's own will hunt — it already does.
- A fire laid for a tired neighbour that never sits: the speaker is asked to the fire by `BotBeckon` on its own
  twenty-minute clock, so some fires will burn with `0 came to it`. `fire` finished with nobody come is the sign;
  the camp's `Lonely` counter already says it. If common, point at the nearest fire (`offer:fire:near`, words) only.
- `called into a company` against the company then doing nothing: a bored prowler called into a company that has no
  enemy is let go by the squad's own idle clock and the enlistment ends `KeptOut`; the line prints both.
- `Unanswered` against `Asked`: how often a line found nobody fit, on the clock, hostile or shunned. With two listeners
  at most, two minutes per listener and twenty per pair, the ceiling is about thirty answers an hour per listener; the
  expected rate is a few answers a minute shard-wide. If `OnClock` dominates, the clocks are the limit and may be loosened
  in `bot-social.json`; if `Hostile` dominates once wars stand, that is the order working.
- Left open: a mood said *to* a particular bot (the lines are to whoever is there); the minds' bots (`BotMind`) answer
  as everybody does; no mood for the Baron beyond his grief; `mood:*` lines in the live `bot-voice.json` are the file's
  (the three old keys stay; the seven new come from the code until the file names them).

**01.10.2026 · build 386 (written by Opus) · The paths headline is the walkers' own count: beside a goal the ground refuses is arriving**
- *Measured, thirty minutes after the wipe on build 385 (11:33–12:02):* the dashboard's paths share read 92.0 % (42655 searches, 39249 reached, 3396 partial) while every purpose stood at 99.3–99.9 % (fixed 99.92, chase 99.74, flight 99.69, station 99.26). The `Getting about:` line of the same window: 3391 "plans one tile short taken as arriving", 3373 partials "going somewhere within 32 tiles", 2298 "ended no nearer than they started, the average one 2 tiles out". The fresh population fights in melee near the towns; a search for a creature standing on a rock or a station on a wall-top is Partial to the search engine, and the walker, already beside it, arrives (BotWalk.Plan, "one tile off and no way onto it is arriving", 29.09.2026).
- *Decision:* the headline (`/api/state` `paths.share`, and the dashboard's history) is `BotWalk.WalkerReached / BotWalk.WalkerSearches` — the four purposes summed, beside counting as reached exactly as each purpose already counted it. The raw search share stays as `paths.searchShare`, with `walkerSearches`, `walkerReached` and `besides` beside it. Nothing a bot does changes; the 99 % is asked of the same definition the per-purpose shares have used since build 270.
- *Why it is not a flattering number:* a walk that ends beside a goal it cannot stand on is how the errand ends in the game (a blow lands from beside, a bandage is wound from beside); counting it as a road not found made the headline fall whenever more bots fought, which is the opposite of what it is meant to show. The partial searches that end far from their goal are still failures in both counts.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · Births lean: the same points, towards one skill of the class's own**
- *Patrick, 01.10.2026 ~00:50 (night plan v2, point 7, translated):* "All our bots start at the same level now; add a little randomness. Some bots may start with more Swordsmanship if they are swordsmen, but put fewer points into other talents. Gatherers who love digging put more into Mining, to dig more and better ore faster. Crafters put the most into Blacksmithy, Fletching and the other producing trades, to give the market what it asks for sooner." Point 2 of the same plan: "check again that crafters can make armour from other metals; this matters."
- *Measured:* `BotMobile.Learn` deals every non-seasoned bot 50 / 30 / 20 to its three highest targets in declared order and `LearnWeapon` gives the rolled weapon 50, so every bot of a class was born identical: a crafter at Mining 50, Blacksmithy 30, Tailoring 20, blade 50, Tinkering and Fletching 0. The engine's coloured-metal floors are on the Blacksmithy *base* (`CraftItem.cs:647`): dull copper 65, shadow iron 70, copper 75, up to valorite 99. Live build 384 (`/api/state`, 10:45): the 9 crafters stand at Blacksmithy 36–49 after a day, with blades at 64–100 and Mining at 62–98. Only the 3 Architects (seasoned, 78 at birth) are at 80–82. Sonnet's 384 read (`sonnet-trade-behaviour-384.md`): 93 % of 1,709 mine stints dig coloured ore. Smiths' "ordering N ingots" decisions were Iron 180, Copper 4, Shadow Iron 3.
- *Why:* a crafter's training goes where its work goes. Crafters hunt and mine, and the anvil was mostly out of metal (85 % of looks "short of metal"), so Blacksmithy climbed slowest of their skills. A smith born at 30 needs 35 points at the anvil before the first coloured bar it holds is of any use. In practice it never got there, while the island's miners dug coloured ore almost exclusively.
- *Options:* (a) a bigger birth allowance for everyone (not what was asked: "fewer points into other talents", and it would raise every class's start); (b) a fixed specialist sub-class per trade (a second list of classes that drifts from the first); (c) one temperament per newborn, drawn from the class's own declared leanings and paid for out of its own birth points. Taken: (c).
- *Decision:*
  - **The data.** `BotClasses/BotLeaning.cs` (new) is a record: name, skill (or "the rolled weapon"), weight, band, an optional material ladder (`BotTier`: Metal, Leather, Ore) and the floors the leaning keeps. `BotClass.Leanings` holds each class's set, written in its `Defaults()`.
  - **The mechanism.** `BotPopulation/BotBirth.cs` (new) applies it in `BotMobile.Become`, after `LearnWeapon` and before `BotProgress.Restore`.
    - The draw is seeded by FNV-1a over name and class into SplitMix64, so it is reproducible per name and not `Utility.Random` or `string.GetHashCode`.
    - The leaning's skill is raised to a whole-point value drawn in its band, never above the class's target, 100 or the skill's cap.
    - The cost comes out of the other dealt skills in proportion to what each can spare, working in tenths of a point. Each skill spares down to the floor its leaning names, otherwise down to `KeepShare` (0.5) of its birth value. The class's `MainSkill` spares nothing unless the leaning names a floor for it, so a healer's Healing, an archer's Archery, a mage's Magery, a tamer's Taming and a gatherer's Mining are never lowered.
    - Nothing is added. A bot whose other skills cannot pay for the full draw leans less, and is counted.
    - The seasoned classes (Captain, Baron, Architect, Sage) are untouched.
  - **Ladders are read, not copied.** Smith and tailor bands start at the first coloured rung of `DefBlacksmithy` / `DefTailoring` `CraftSubRes`. The digger's band starts at the first `Mining.OreAndStone` vein that asks for skill. All three are 65 in this era.
  - **The leanings by class** (weights, then bands):

    | Class | Leanings (weight, band) |
    |---|---|
    | Warrior | blade 5 (rolled weapon 56–72), even 1 |
    | Archer | marksman 5 (Archery 58–74), even 1 |
    | WarriorArcher | marksman 4 (56–70, under its 75 target), even 1 |
    | WarriorMage | blade 2 (56–66, under 70), spellsword 2 (Magery 56–68), even 1 |
    | Brawler | Wrestling 4 (58–72), even 1 |
    | Mage | archmage 4 (Magery 58–72), scribe 1 (Inscribe 36–40, paid by Meditation alone because Magery never pays), even 1 |
    | Healer | mender 4 (Healing 58–72), even 1 |
    | Tamer | beastmaster 3 (Taming 58–70), marksman 1 (56–66), even 1 |
    | Gatherer | digger 4 (Mining 65–80), woodsman 1 (Lumberjacking 45–60), even 1 |
    | Crafter | always leans: smith 6 (Blacksmithy 65–75), bowyer 2 (Fletching 55–65, crossbows at 60), tailor 1 (Tailoring 65–75: spined at 65, LeatherLegs 66.3, LeatherChest 70.5), tinker 1 (Tinkering 45–55: every tool at 40 + the crafts' 5-point margin) |

    Crafter floors: Mining keeps 40, because smelting is a Mining check. Blacksmithy (its main skill) keeps 10 when the crafter leans elsewhere. The blade goes to half (crafter class note: "it carries a blade because everything on this island does").
  - **Resulting births** (the C# arithmetic mirrored over all 200 names in `bot-names.json`, weapon fixed to Swords):

    | Class | Leaning | Share | Skills at birth |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | Crafter | smith | 56 % | Blacksmithy 65–75, Mining 40–42, Tailoring 10–12, blade 25–31 |
    | Crafter | bowyer | 22 % | Fletching 55–65, Blacksmithy 10–13 |
    | Crafter | tinker | 13 % | Tinkering 45–55 |
    | Crafter | tailor | 10 % | Tailoring 65–74 |
    | Gatherer | digger | 69 % | Mining 65–80, Lumberjacking 21–26, Tactics 14–17, blade 35–42 |
    | Gatherer | woodsman | 14 % | Lumberjacking 45–60, Mining 50 |
    | Gatherer | even | 18 % | as the class deals |
    | Warrior | blade | 84 % | weapon 56–72, Tactics 39–47, Anatomy 23–28, Healing 16–19 |
    | Archer | marksman | 83 % | Archery 58–74, Tactics 38–46 |
    | Mage | archmage | 66 % | Magery 58–72, Inscribe 17–25, Meditation 11–17 |
    | Mage | scribe | 20 % | Inscribe 36–40, Magery 50 |
    | Healer | mender | 76 % | Healing 58–72, Anatomy 17–25, Magery 11–17 |
- *Counted:*
  - **One line per birth:** `X the Crafter was born leaning smith: Blacksmithy 30 to 71, Mining 50.0 to 41.0, Tailoring 20.0 to 10.0, Swordsmanship 50.0 to 27.0`. An even birth says "born even, as its class deals it".
  - **`births:` in the five-minute `Rest:` line (`BotBeat`):** born this session from a class's deal; how many leaned (and points moved), even, and trimmed; smiths born at or above the first coloured metal's floor against those below it; and every class's leanings by count, e.g. `Crafter: smith 4, bowyer 1, tinker 1; Gatherer: digger 7, …`.
- *Expected (first hour after the wipe, 80 bots):* `births:` shows about 80 born, about 65 leaned, `0 trimmed`, `0 below it`, and about 3–4 crafter smiths at or above 65. The forge's new `hammers by the best metal their Blacksmithy opens:` reads Dull Copper, Shadow Iron and Copper from the first beat (the Architects add Copper/Bronze). The forge's `pieces by metal` shows coloured pieces within the first hour of smiths holding coloured bars. `Resolve:` forge share holds at ≥ 95 %.
- *Risks / watch:*
  1. **Smiths are no longer novices.** `BotLadder.Novice` reads `MainSkill < 50`, so a crafter born a smith (Blacksmithy 65+) is not a novice. It fights to the ordinary failing fraction and may be given ground that has hurt somebody (`BotHunter`), with a blade of 25–31. Diggers were never novices (Mining 50 is not under 50); their blade falls from 50 to 35–42. Watch deaths by class for Crafter and Gatherer in the first two hours. `dial BotBirth.KeepShare 0.6` keeps more of the blade, and smiths still reach 68. From 0.65 smiths fall short of 65 and `below it` counts them.
  2. **Diluted secondary skills.** Healers lose Anatomy (30 → 17–25), mages lose Inscribe (30 → 17–25) and archers lose Tactics (50 → 38–46). This is the "fewer points into other talents" Patrick asked for, but it slows a mage's scrolls and a healer's heal amount at the start.
  3. **Small sample.** With only 6 crafters in the 80, a seeded draw can deal no smith at all (0.4⁶ ≈ 0.4 %). The Architects (Blacksmithy 78, seasoned) still work dull copper to copper. `births:` shows it at once.
  4. **Duplicate names.** Two bots with one name and one class lean the same way, by construction.
  5. **Off switch.** `dial BotBirth.Leans false` puts births back to the class's deal; bots already born keep their skills.
- *Status:* attempt.
- *Code:*

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · Coloured metals in the hand-to-hand market: a bar no shopkeeper prices was never shown, so no smith ever asked for one; the forge now names its metal**
- *Patrick, 01.10.2026 (night plan v2, point 2, translated):* "check again whether crafters can make armour from other metals. This matters."
- *Measured / read:*
  - **The craft path works, as Fable found.**
    - `BotAnvil.Best` takes the dearest metal held whose `RequiredSkill` is at or under the Blacksmithy *base*. `BotForge.Working` passes it to `BotAnvil.Swing`, which calls `CraftItem.Craft(…, typeRes, …)`. The engine maps the recipe's iron to `typeRes` (`CraftItem.cs:641`) and refuses only under the base floor (`:647`).
    - `GetSuccessChance` reads the main skill alone, so the metal does not change the odds.
    - The worn piece is chosen by `ArmorRating`, which in UOR adds the metal's bonus (`BaseArmor.cs:317`, dull copper +2 … valorite +16).
  - **The new market blocked the metal before it reached the anvil.**
    - No shopkeeper in this era buys or sells a coloured ingot. Only `IronIngot` is in `SBBlacksmith`/`SBSmithTools`, and `GenericSellInfo.IsSellable` matches the exact type.
    - `BotShopkeep.Opening` opens a kind at the shelf, else at `Worth(kind, PaidFor(…))`. For a coloured bar both are 0 until a smith has bid or a trade has happened, so `Count` drops it (`ask <= 0`) and it is never shown.
    - `BotAnvil.Plentiful` reads only `BotShopkeep.Showing`, so it never saw a coloured bar. An empty smith's `Best` therefore fell back to iron, and `BotBullion` ordered iron.
    - On build 384 the auction listed coloured bars at a guess, which is how its board showed 622. Even then the smiths' orders were Iron 180 against Copper 4 and Shadow Iron 3 (Sonnet), because no crafter had the base.
    - On the wipe build both halves would have been closed: no smith born able to work the bar, and no shop able to show it.
  - **No log named the metal of any crafted piece.** Endings read "3 Mace made", so Patrick's question could not be answered from the shard.
- *Decision:*
  1. **`BotAnvil.Reckon(metal)`.** A coloured bar's price before the island has traded one is iron's price (`BotMarket.Worth(IronIngot, BotBullion.Guess)`) × (1 + `ColouredPremium` × floor / 100): dull copper 1.65×, bronze 1.8×, valorite 1.99×. It is 0 for iron and for anything that is not a smith's metal, so every other kind is priced as before. It is read on both sides of the meeting:
     - `BotShopkeep.Opening`: when no shopkeeper pays for the sample, the bar opens at `Worth(kind, Reckon)`, so shops show coloured bars and `Plentiful` sees them;
     - `BotBullion`: the offer is `Worth(kind, max(Guess, Reckon))`, so a smith's want is never under the shop's ask for the bar it can work.

     A smith born at 65+ with an empty pack then orders the commonest workable coloured metal on show, through the carriers (`BotCourier`) or by walking to the shop (`BotPatron`). It keeps it (`BotAnvil.Keep`) and beats it out (`Best`).
  2. **The forge names its metal.** `BotForge` remembers the metal of each swing (`_swungMetal`) and books every piece found made under it (`Book`), per stint and since load.
     - The ending line is `Edda beat out 2 PlateGorget of Bronze in 6 attempts: …`. The stint result is `2 PlateGorget of Bronze made, 1 for an order and 1 kept`. Mixed metals read `Bronze (2) and Iron (1)`.
     - The smith's summary (`Needs:` → `BotSmith.Describe` → `BotForge.Describe`) gains `pieces by metal: Iron 120, Dull Copper 9 (9 of 129 in a coloured metal)` and `hammers by the best metal their Blacksmithy opens: Iron 2, Dull Copper 2, Shadow Iron 1, Copper 3`. The second is counted over `BotPopulation.Bots` and `Away` every five minutes, for classes that `Want` Blacksmithy.
  3. **The births** (entry above) put a smith at 65–75 on the base from the first second. The first stint holding a coloured bar makes coloured armour.
- *Not changed:*
  - **Finished goods are priced by kind.** `BotShopkeep`'s book, `BotMarket.Worth` and `BotGlut.Yield` key on the type, so a bronze gorget is offered and counted at the gorget's price. A buyer still gets the better piece for it and wears it first, because the rating carries the metal. Pricing by item would need the shop book and the handover keyed by resource, so it is left for a later wave.
  - **Fable's `BotGlut` is untouched.** Its risk 3 is now live in a different shape. With `Reckon`, coloured bars are *shown*, so `Showing` adds them to the glut's pile and a miner's coloured bars count at the floor until a smith asks for them. The births are what turns that around: smiths able to ask exist from the first minute. Watch `Balance:` for DullCopper/ShadowIron/Copper leaving the glutted list once `hammers … Dull Copper/Shadow Iron/Copper` is non-zero; Agapite (90) and above stay glutted by design.
  - **Coloured leather:** the era has it (`DefTailoring` sub-resources spined 65 / horned 80 / barbed 99; `BaseCreature` drops spined hides; UOR rating +10/+13/+16). The bots' tailoring path sews only `typeof(Leather)`, and on 384 `SpinedLeather` was condemned as worthless (`The market:` line). The tailor's birth band is set on that ladder (65+) so a tailor is ready, but a coloured-leather chain (`BotSew`/`BotTailor` choosing the hide, a want for it, a price) is not built here, because those files are balance-patched. **Coloured woods** are ML-only (`Lumberjacking` adds oak/ash/yew only under `Core.ML`), so this era has none.
- *Expected:*
  - `The board:` / shops show DullCopper/ShadowIron/Copper ingots within the first hour of the miners' shifts.
  - `Needs:` "ordered metal" includes coloured kinds, and the smiths' share of iron orders drops well under Sonnet's 180-to-7.
  - `pieces by metal` shows coloured pieces after the first carrier delivery to a smith.
- *Risks / watch:*
  1. `ColouredPremium` is a guess on top of iron's guess. If shops hold coloured bars that smiths can work and `Bot shops:` sells none, check that the want's offer meets the ask (`BotPatron` "dearer than they would pay"). `dial BotAnvil.ColouredPremium 0` prices them as iron.
  2. A smith with 20 iron in the pack orders nothing (`Stocked`) and works iron; coloured bars come only when its iron runs low. By design: availability first.
  3. `Hands()` walks the population on every `Describe`; that is ≤ 210 bots and cheap, but the debugger can ask for it too.
- *Status:* attempt.
- *Code:*
  - `BotCraft/BotAnvil.cs` (`Rung`, `Reckon`, `ColouredPremium`, `Named`, `Hands`)
  - `BotCraft/BotForge.cs` (`_swungMetal`, `Book`, `Metals`, `ByMetal`, the ending line and `Describe`/`Forget`)
  - `BotShopkeep/BotShopkeep.cs` (`Opening`, one line)
  - `BotShops/BotBullion.cs` (the offer, one line)
  - `BotShopkeep/README.md`
  - Both patches apply cleanly together (`randstart2.patch` dry-run on a fresh base-night2 and on base-night2 + `balance.patch`), and the combined tree builds.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · The Trader: a merchant class, seven of the eighty, born in Britain**
- *Patrick, 30.09.2026, night, point 5 (translated):* "Traders, a new faction: they like buying in other towns, trading at the market, offering their services reselling goods and services. The result of their work must be healthy demand for products and supplying it in time. Once well off they may sail to other towns to buy materials for other bots." *Plan v2, 01.10.2026, point 3:* "99 % for traders: they feel the market and follow the needs. Give them a fun feature: write orders into a book and strike them out when delivered."
- *Measured (the 384 trade baseline, `sonnet-trade-behaviour-384.md`, 00:42–10:30, 692 bot-hours):* RawRibs is 46 % of all units wanted and 17 % of it was filled (cooks offer 12gp a rib, `Corvin wants 13 RawRibs and has put 156gp down`; a butcher sells at 16 and buys at 8); units wanted filled overall 58.8 %; 59.5 % of economic bots hold under 100gp, median 70gp. Fable's market review: about 65 % of bots live beyond a carrier's 400 tiles of each other, so hand-to-hand trade between towns has no carrier at all.
- *Decision:* `BotTrader` (`BotClasses/BotTrader.cs`): role `Producer`, new flag `BotClass.Neutral` true, Str/Dex/Int 45/40/15, skills declared Tactics, Arms Lore, Healing, Anatomy (opening 50/30/20 after the rolled weapon's 50 — armed for the road), main skill **Arms Lore** (ItemID is everybody's at 100, so the appraiser's mark is the other lore; trained by a check on every lot bought and handed over, so rank follows trade), kit `BotArsenal.Melee(100)`, no tools. Mix (`bot-population.json`): Trader 7, taken from Warrior 12→10, Archer 11→9, Mage 9→8, WarriorArcher 6→5, Tamer 5→4; total stays 80, and `BotGrowth` draws newcomers by the same weights. `BotRelocate.StayHome` gains `Trader`: they live in Britain, where the market and their shop are, and go out from there.
- *Why a producer:* the levy, delve, harrow, tollman, robber, skulker, proving and tourney all pass producers over already, so most of the neutrality comes for nothing; `BotShopkeeper.Merchant` reads the role, so a trader keeps shop at Britain's bank with whatever it could not hand over. `BotGrowth.OfRole` now skips classes no guild may take in (trader, and the architect it already wrongly sent), so a guild short of a producer is never sent a trader.
- *Watch:* the boot line `Bot classes: …` counts fifteen; `byClass.Trader` on `/api/state` is 7 after the wipe.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · Neutral in wars: no guild, no company, no toll**
- *Patrick, 30.09.2026, answering "traders belong to the wars?" (translated):* neutral in wars — not attacked in guild wars and not taking part in them.
- *Why no guild, rather than a traders' guild:* every war on this shard is between guilds — `BotRegard` opinions, `Hostile`/`AtWar`, `BotFeuder`'s rallies and quarrels (it needs the bot's guild and the other's), a war company's attackers (`BotSquad.Consider` asks `AtWar`), `BotWar` kills and plunder, envoys and the duke's meetings, the bailiff's strangers. A guild of traders would be one more guild those could quarrel with, and each would need a test; a trader in no guild is outside all of them by construction. Its home town is Britain, not a guild seat.
- *Decision:* `BotGuilds.Barred` holds `Trader` and `Outside` also reads `Class.Neutral`. `BotTrading.Neutral(m)` (dial `NeutralInWars`) closes the two doors a guild does not: companies — `BotSquads.Form` and `Join` (the one door in, so levy, harrow, delve, press, muster and war companies alike) refuse it, counted `CompanyRefused`; `BotEnlist.Propose` and `BotMuster.Propose` offer it nothing (`BotTrading.Passes`, counted `CallsPassed`), so it never walks to a company that would refuse it — and tolls: `BotToll.Rate` is nought, `Exempted` waives and counts (`TollWaived`), no warden is sent. Self-defence stays a reflex; rescues only ever fight creatures. A bandit may still rob a trader on the road: that is a crime, not a war.
- *Watch:* `Traders: … neutral in wars: N company doors shut, M calls not offered, K tolls waived`; no `X fell in with company` line for a trader; `Guilds: …` excused count up by the traders.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · The haul: only against a spoken want, from wherever it is cheapest, at a price the buyer agrees to**
- *Why:* Patrick's balance rule (plan v2, point 8): no flooding — after a pile of offers and zero demand, hunting pays better. A trader that bought on spec would be the worst flooder on the island. So its demand is `BotMarket.Wants` and nothing else: no open want, no haul, and it hunts like any bot (Patrick, 30.09: poor bots hunt; no kits).
- *Decision:* proposer `BotHauler` ("Trader"), deed `BotHaul` (kind `haul`). A want is taken when open, at least `FreshMs` (60 s) old so the carriers within reach go first, not a trader's (no carousel), not one the trader wants itself, the buyer alive, not on ground `BotPeril` calls overwhelming, not past a way through. Sources weighed by profit a minute: its own pack, its own box at a bank, a bot's shop within reach (`BotShopkeep.Best`, coin stays on the island), a shopkeeper in any town (cheapest goods plus road at the shard's price of a minute, then vetted by `BotShops.Nearest`), or a gathering (next entry). Price: the buyer's offer when it pays `LeastMarkup` (15 %) over cost; otherwise carriage — the least price plus `CarriageShare` (half) of the way up to the buyer's own alternative (its walk to its nearest counter and back at `BotShopkeep.WalkGold`), never over `MostMarkup` (double) cost, never under the offer; the buyer says "Agreed" in the world chat; units are what it can pay for. Up to `MostOrders` (3) buyers of the same kind within `BatchTiles` (200) on one purchase. Steadfast and `Committed` from the first line: the book is the trader's word. The want's units are reserved (`BotWant.Reserve`) so no second carrier walks for them. Leftovers go to another open want for the kind (`Adopt`) or stay as stock for its shop. Takings are the margin; leftovers count as made at cost.
- *Market core, minimal and separate:* new `BotMarket/IBotWantCarrier.cs`; `BotWant.Sweep` asks the interface instead of `as BotDeliver` (a haul's reservation was otherwise swept on the next beat); `BotDeliver` implements it (one line). `BotShopper`'s far-counter ask keeps standing while a carrier is bringing it (`Coming > 0`) instead of withdrawing at ten minutes under a haul already on its way. `BotUnload.Needed` keeps a haul's owed goods in the pack (`BotTrading.Keep`). Nothing in `BotMarket.cs` itself changed; no reference to the balance agent's `BotGlut` (not in this base) — a haul buys only what a want asks, which adds no pile, and its gathering want is counted once in `BotMarket.Asked` because the far want it answers is reserved.
- *Watch:* `Traders: … hauls: N taken, M finished … (X% finished)` and the will's `haul` tally in `Resolve:` (the authoritative share; aim 99 %); `sold: H handovers … margin …gp (C gp of it carriage A buyers agreed to)`; the passed-over buckets — `Thin` large and `Offered` small means prices leave no margin (lower `LeastMarkup` or `LeastProfit`), `Fresh` large is expected.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · The gathering: a trader buys from the bots of its own town for a buyer no carrier there reaches**
- *Why:* the ribs. Hunters everywhere carry ribs; a cook 800 tiles away is beyond every carrier, so the hunters peddle them to a butcher at 8 and the cook waits, raising its 12 until it gives up. A trader in the hunters' town is the bridge: it says "Buying 13 raw ribs at 10" at its town's bank, the town's carriers bring them hand to hand (each a `BotDeliver` of theirs — better than the butcher's 8), and it carries them to the cook at 12. The same works for a maker's spare piece. And the round trip Patrick asked for falls out of it: a trader that has just delivered in Yew looks from Yew, a Britain cook's want is then one no carrier in Yew reaches, so it gathers in Yew and carries home — "buying in other towns".
- *Decision:* source `BotHaulFrom.Gather`, offered only when the buyer is past `BotCourier.Reach` of the trader or on another land and the trader stands in a town with a bank; bid = the buyer's offer less `LeastMarkup`. The haul walks to `BotShopkeep.BankNear(town square)`, says the want (`BotMarket.Ask`), stands `Still` for `GatherMs` (5 min; up to twice that while a carrier is on its way) or until covered, withdraws, tops up at the nearest counter when it sells under the orders' prices, trims the orders to what it has otherwise. Weighed in the proposer at `GatherYield` (half). The meetings book the trader's payment aside (as for any buyer mid-work); the haul puts it back (`BotYield.Aside(-paid)`), so its takings are its true margin.
- *Watch:* `gathered … N gatherings, U things brought for G gp, E brought nothing, T topped up at a counter`; E close to N means the town holds none of the kind (raise `GatherYield`'s caution or shorten `GatherMs`). `The market:` deliveries' `found the want met or withdrawn` should not jump (a gathering withdraws only after its window, longer while carriers come).

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · The order book: written when taken, struck when handed over or given up**
- *Decision:* `BotOrderBook` (`BotTraders/BotOrderBook.cs`), a `BlueBook` subclass (`[SerializationGenerator(0, false)]`, not writable, not movable, blessed), made in the trader's pack at its first order. Page one: written, delivered, struck, open, margin, next number. One page per open order: `#12 OPEN`, for whom, how many of what, the price (with the buyer's own offer when carriage was agreed above it), when (`dd.MM HH:mm`), in which town, where it is bought. Then the closed orders, newest first, `BookHistory` (40): `X #12 Odile` / ` 20 leather` / ` done 180gp (+60)` or ` struck: the buyer died`. `BotOrders` keeps it in memory and rewrites the pages at each change; the first write after a boot reads the book's own pages back, so counts and history survive a restart and whatever was open is struck "the island slept". A dead buyer is waited for `DeadWaitMs` (3 min; bots rise about a minute after falling) before its line is struck. A GM opens the trader's pack and reads it like any book.
- *Watch:* `X wrote order #N into its book: …` and `X struck order #N out of its book: … — reason`; `Traders: … book: L lines written, D struck as delivered, S struck unfulfilled (reasons), O open now`. Delivered/written is the honest service rate of the traders.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · Sailing when well off**
- *Decision:* a source or buyer no road or gate reaches is weighed (`BotHauler.Road`, `BotSea.Plan`) and taken only by a trader for which `BotTrading.CanSail` holds: `Sails`, the sea ready, and a ship already owned or worth `SailWealth` (12,000gp — a small ship is 10,177 at the shipwright, and a haul needs capital after it) and `BotSea.CanSail`. The leg is the ordinary `BotVoyage` (ship bought the first time, dock, lane, landing), run inside the haul until it lands; afloat the haul is `Still`. Below the threshold traders go by land and gates (`BotGates.Joined` counts gates), and a want across the water is passed over (`Unjoined`).
- *Watch:* `sea: N sailings, L landed, X lost`; nought for the first hours after the wipe is expected (purse 400).

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · `Traders:` every five minutes**

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (Fable review) · The traders and the balance: no counter into a glut, a gathering is not demand, leftovers at the glut's price**
- *Patrick, 01.10.2026 ~00:50 (plan v2, point 8):* do not let the bots flood the market; the bar is 95 %. The traders agent could not see the balance (`BotMarket/BotGlut.cs`, Fable's own patch of the same night), so the haul was wired to the market and not to the balance.
- *Measured (read, not run — no trader exists on 384):* `BotHauler.Weigh` weighed the island's cheapest shopkeeper for every want whatever the pile: with twenty daggers on the bots' shops and one archer asking, the trader would carry a twenty-first in from the provisioner with its margin on it. `BotGlut.Read` summed `BotMarket.Asked` over every want, so a trader's five-minute gathering want for forty ribs at the bank turned RawRibs to ×1 for the makers' choice and `Yield` while the far want it answered was reserved and read as nothing — and the piece a maker started for it would be finished after the trader had gone. `BotHaul.Keep` counted leftovers as made at cost, so a haul that bought eighty and handed over twenty read to the ledger as well as one that handed over eighty.
- *Decision:* three hooks and no more. (1) `BotHauler.Weigh` and `BotHaul.TopUp` pass a shopkeeper's counter over while `BotGlut.Glutted(kind)` (factor ≤ `Shunned` 0.34), counted `BotTrading.Glutted`; a bot's shop, the trader's own stock and a gathering — all of which drain the pile — are still weighed. (2) `BotGlut.Asked` (private) walks `BotMarket.Wants` and leaves out the units a `Neutral` class asks for; the carriers still read the trader's want and bring it what they hold; what the trader then hands over counts as sold between bots at the meeting. Units left out are summed over readings as `BotGlut.TraderUnitsLeftOut` and printed in `Balance:`. (3) `BotHaul.Keep` reads `Made = min(left × cost, BotGlut.Yield(kind, left, cost))`. Nothing in the trader's prices, the buyer's offer or the meeting changes.
- *Watch:* `Traders:` `Glutted` nought in the first half hour (no pile yet) and rising only when `Balance:` names the kind; `Balance:` `units of traders' gathering wants left out` > 0 after the first gathering; glutted kinds not flipping to ×1 while a trader stands at the bank; `Leftover` against `handed over` in `Traders:`.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (Fable review) · A struck want is left alone: the trader's shun list**
- *Measured (read):* the haul's strikes for "could not catch up with the buyer" (`ChaseMs`, eight minutes after a buyer that keeps walking), "refused at the meeting", "across the water, and no ship" and "no way through to the buyer" marked nothing on the want — only the last filed a ledger `Beware` — so the next look twenty seconds later (`LookMs`) re-took the same want and chased the same hunter for another eight minutes, for as long as the want stood (about a hundred minutes). A carousel of one trader and one buyer, and the share of finished hauls paid for it.

Called by `BotHaul` on the four strikes above; "the buyer could not pay" withdraws the want itself.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (Fable review) · The traders reviewed: what was checked and found sound, and the wipe clears their memory**
- *Checked and sound (not changed):* gold moves only through the engine and the market's own hands (`BotHandover.Exchange`, `BotShopkeep.Serve`, `BotShops.Buy`, `BotMarket.FromBank`) — the haul books nothing, charged = paid + refunded, `Made` is gold-equivalent and never coin; a gathering's meetings are `BotDeliver`s of the carriers and book `Aside(+takings)` on the trader, which `Gathered` undoes with `Aside(−paid)` so the haul's own cost counts; every reservation has a release on every ending and `Paused` keeps it until `Stale`; `IBotWantCarrier` for the sweep; no trader hauls to a trader's want (`ToTraders`) or its own; neutrality closes by construction (no guild) plus one company door (`BotSquads.Join`, asked before the press) and the toll, and the producer role keeps a trader out of the raid's and outlaw's target lists, the robbers', skulkers' and The Shadow's rolls, the harrow, the bailiff, the proving ground and the tourney; `BotOrderBook` is a `partial` `BlueBook` with `[SerializationGenerator(0, false)]` and `[Constructible]` like `BotGuildDoor`, immovable, blessed, in the BotAI namespace so neither the porter nor `Merchandise` moves it; the class mix sums to 80; the hot path is a cast and a ≤ 3 loop in the porter and a 20-second-rested look for a trader.
- *Decision:* `BotHand.ResetPopulation` calls `BotTrading.Forget()` after `BotMarket.Reset()`: the books go with the packs, but the pages held in memory were keyed by the serials of deleted bots, with the counters and the looks' quiet clock.
- *Left as designed, to watch:* a far-counter buyer now waits for a haul however long it takes (bounded by `MostHaulMs` 45 min and the sweep — `dial BotTrading.MostHaulMs 1800000` if `WaitedFar` balloons); makers may still take a gathering want as an order (`BotMarket.Demand`); a duel has no role gate (a sport, not a war); `BotGuilds.Outside` reads `Class.Neutral` whatever the `NeutralInWars` dial says.
- *Verdict:* safe to deploy and wipe on, with the three entries above in. Review notes: `scratchpad/agents/traders-review.md`.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · The leash is on the quarry's running, not on the hunter's road; a jump is not a chase**
- *Patrick, 01.10 ~01:00:* «hunting means they hunt everything that can be killed or is hostile to them, outside the towns» — and hunting must not sag.
- *Measured:* 223 of 1877 hunts (11.9 %) failed "X drew it N tiles past where it was found and was let go". 124 were exactly 51 tiles and most of those one loop: Belthorn, Cirdan and Gerdrun took a ghoul from (1980, 2932) 23 times between 02:38 and 09:44, walked the road north to (1999, 2831) every time and let it go there 0.4 minutes in — the leash measured the hunter's own displacement, so a way round to a creature that never moved read as being dragged. 49 more were 81–2912 tiles (29 over 1000: "a skeleton drew it 2909 tiles", Falk 01:01:57): a hunt put down for a company's call or a flight and taken up again through a gate, the leash still measured from where it began.
- *Decision (`BotSlay.Closing`, `Stale`, `Resumed`; dials `FarLeash` 3, `JumpTiles` 40):* the leash (50) bounds the quarry's own distance from where it was found (or from where it stood when the hunt was taken up again), and never applies to a quarry fighting this bot or already fought by it; the hunter's own displacement keeps a far bound of `FarLeash × Leash` past the walk out (150 tiles; the 737 that wrote the leash on 09.09 stays impossible), and `CapMs` still bounds time. A move of more than `JumpTiles` between two closing beats re-measures the leash. A hunt put down and about to be taken up again whose quarry (or its corpse) is further than `Reach + Leash` from the bot is settled "not taken up again: X is N tiles off now" through a new `BotDeed.Stale` hook read by `BotWill.Unpause` (dropped, not failed).
- *Watch (hunter's line, "the hunt itself"):* `Slipped` "quarry let go for running 50 tiles", `Dragged` "for drawing the hunter 150 past its walk out", `Unleashed` "hunts kept past the old leash", `Rebased`, `StaleResumes`. Expected: leash failures from ~11.9 % of hunts to under 3 %, none over 500 tiles, no bot with more than a handful on one creature.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by an Opus agent) · An archer gives ground only to what it can leave behind**
- *Measured:* 117 hunts (6.2 %) and a few rescues failed "X would not go down: N% left and not a scratch in 45s (holding Bow, 50–150 arrows, 1–4 tiles off, 3–149 kites, moving|still, in sight True)" — timber/grey wolves, black/grizzly bears, bulls, cows, great harts, orcs; never a zombie. Ammunition, sight and range were all present. A bow fires only after a full second standing still (`BaseRanged.OnSwing`, `StillMs`), and these creatures step every 0.2 s (`ActiveSpeed`), as fast as a running bot (`movement.delay.runFoot` 200): backing off one never opens the distance, so the archer is never still and never shoots. "5564 beats shooters had moved too recently to fire" in the companies say the same.
- *Decision (`BotSlay.GainsGround`, `Stand`; dials `OutpaceShare` 1.25, `FootStepMs` 200, `MountStepMs` 100, `PlantMs` 3000):* an archer kites or backs off only from a quarry whose step is at least a quarter slower than its own run; and once backing off has left the quarry inside `TooClose` for `PlantMs`, it plants for the rest of that fight. Standing, it finishes any back-off walk still under way (a deed answering Work does not stop the walk by itself) and shoots at the range it has — a bow has no least range. Casters keep their own rule.
- *Watch:* `Bows:` "N beats an archer stood and shot rather than give ground…, P fights an archer stopped backing off in…"; hunts "would not go down … holding Bow" from 6.2 % toward 1.5 %.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by Fable) · The balance: a glutted kind is a low price to whoever makes one more of it**
- *Patrick, 01.10.2026 ~00:50 (night plan v2, point 8):* Special attention to trade balance: do not let bots flood the market; after a pile of offers and zero demand it must pay them better to go hunting or join a company. A hard architectural decision for Fable; the bar is 95 %. Standing answers: poor bots hunt, never kits or handouts; orders are hand to hand (`BotMarket`, build 384 review).
- *Measured (`session-2026-10-01_00-42.log`, build 384 with the old auction, cumulative at 10:17):* tinkering — 522 stints ended, 1,338 tools made, **0 to order and 1,310 put out unsold**, while 5,360 looks "found every tool stocked"; the forge — 136 stints to order against **900 on spec**, 389 pieces beaten out; weaving — 5,745 cloth put out, 0 to orders; the shops — 409 shifts ran their eight minutes and **328 of them sold nothing**, 38,734 looks "held nothing the island is short of or has money down for"; the market — **26,938 things stayed in their sellers' hands** for want of a lot and 4,105 their makers put out past the cap; the board's metal read 945 ingots of seven kinds, 622 of them coloured (copper 292, dull copper 166, agapite 109, gold 20, valorite 9) while 9,075 smiths' looks read "short of metal". `Resolve:` tinker 95 % finished, sew 97 %, cook 95 %, mine 91 %, brew 90 % — the stints finish; what they finish is a pile.
- *Why:* every maker counted its output at `BotMarket.Worth(kind, guess)` — the best standing bid, else the kind's last traded price, else the maker's typed guess — so a piece nobody had asked for and nobody would buy was credited as income at the moment it was made (`BotForge.Made => _made × Worth`, the same in `BotTinker`, `BotBowmake`, `BotSew`, `BotBrew`, `BotFletch`, `BotBake`, `BotWeave`, `BotInscribe`, `BotDig`, `BotChop`). The ledger (`BotLedger.Expect`, `BotCommons.Corrected`) learns from takings, so it learned that making the fortieth dagger pays as well as the first; the choosers (`BotCraftwork.Choose`, `BotThread.Choose`) reached for the hardest recipe for the skill in it, stint after stint, so the pile was always of one kind; and the appraisal (`BotAppraisal.Weigh`) was handed a price, and a price is not a buyer. Nothing on the shard read supply against demand, so nothing could prefer a hunt to a shelf. The same hole priced a miner's agapite — which no smith on the island has the base to work (see the entry below) — at iron's price for the forge.
- *Options:* (a) a hard cap on stock per kind (a veto: a maker with nothing else refuses to work — C3, "factor without a floor is a veto"); (b) lower the makers' priors by hand (a number nobody retunes, and it sinks the wanted goods with the unwanted — C2); (c) a reading of supply against spoken demand per kind, applied to what the maker *reckons* and to what it *chooses*, never to the buyer's price and never as a refusal. Taken: (c).
- *Decision — `BotMarket/BotGlut.cs` (new), read-only to everything but the four hooks:* for a kind, the **pile** is the larger of what the bots' shops show now (`BotShopkeep.Showing`) and what was made this half hour and neither sold between bots nor peddled to a shopkeeper (`BotGlut.Made`/`Sold`/`Peddled`, two rotating fifteen-minute buckets); the **demand** is the units open wants ask for (`BotMarket.Asked`) plus the units sold between bots this half hour. `Factor(kind)` = one while the pile is within a shelf's worth (`Tolerance` 6) or demand covers it, else `(demand + Tolerance) / pile` floored at `Floor` 0.1 — seven of a kind nobody asks for read ×0.86, twenty ×0.30, sixty the floor; a low price, never a veto. Three places bite and no more: (1) **`Yield(kind, units, guess)`** — what a maker counts its output at: the units somebody asks for at the island's price, the rest at the *surplus price*, which is what a shopkeeper pays for one when a peddle has shown it (`Scrap`, learned at `BotShops.Sell` — the one real price of a thing nobody wants) and otherwise the island's price × the factor, floored at one gold-equivalent so a stint that made anything still reads as having produced. Every maker's `Made` reads it; so does the smelt (`BotDig`, now by each metal the fire gave, with a before/after snapshot of the pack's bars) and the woodsman (`BotChop`). The ledger then learns within a few stints that flooding pays little, and hunting, a company or a peddle wins the choice on the ordinary arithmetic — no new rung, no handout. (2) **`Claim(kind, prior)`** — a maker's claim for a stint *on spec* is `Prior × Factor` of the kind it means to make, so the choice sees the pile at once rather than three stints later; `BotSmith` and `BotTailor` now pass the kind they chose into `BotForge`/`BotSew` (`spec`) for this. An order's claim is never marked down: somebody has said it will pay. (3) **`Glutted(kind)`** (factor ≤ `Shunned` 0.34) — `BotCraftwork.Choose` and `BotThread.Choose` keep the hardest glutted kind apart and take it only when it is the only kind they can make; a bid still wins over both. Producers keep producing what is wanted (an open want is demand, so its kind reads ×1), and the shelves carry more kinds instead of more of one. Buyers' offers still come from `BotMarket.Worth`; a want for a glutted kind is paid in full at the meeting. Off by `GlutEnabled` in `bot-market.json` (also `GlutWindowMs`, `GlutFloor`, `GlutTolerance`, `GlutShunned`; live dials `BotGlut.*`), and off, every number is as it was.
- *Counted:* a new `Balance:` line every five minutes (`BotBeat`, after `The market:`): the glutted kinds with pile, asked and factor (worst six); things made, sold between bots and peddled to shopkeepers this half hour and since the world loaded; things made into a glut (counted at the surplus price); stints offered on spec and how many of them for a kind already glutted (`BotGlut.Spec`, called by the smith, tailor, tinker, bowyer, alchemist and fletcher at their on-spec branch); choices on spec turned from a glutted kind (`Steered`); shopkeepers' prices learned. `BotMarket.Reset` clears it with the rest of the market.
- *Expected (first two hours after the wipe):* `on spec … for a kind already glutted` well under a quarter of `on spec` once the shelves fill; `turned from a glutted kind` climbing while `glutted kinds` stays in single figures; `Bot shops:` "sold nothing" under the 80 % of build 384; `Resolve:` the makers' finished shares unchanged (the glut changes prices, not endings) and the makers' share of `taken` falling in favour of hunt, enlist and peddle when the `Balance:` line names their kinds. The 95 % Patrick asks for is read on `Resolve:` by trade — forge, sew, tinker, brew, fletch, cook, weave, inscribe — against a pile that stops growing: the `Balance:` line's "made into a glut" must flatten while those shares hold.
- *Risks / watch:* (1) a crafter whose every kind is glutted and whose purse is full has prowl (8) and the floor claim (12/min for the forge) left; the smith's `Choose` then still makes the pile's kind if it is the only kind — read `turned` against `on spec … glutted`, and `dial BotGlut.Floor 0.05` if the pile still grows. (2) `BotMarket.Asked` is island-wide while a carrier reaches 400 tiles: a Yew hunter's leather reads as wanted by a Britain tailor and counts at the bid; the reach-limited reading would need the bot in every `Made`, which most deeds do not hold — accepted, since the pile reading still bites once the shops fill. (3) Coloured ingots no smith can work read as a glut (shown on the shops, nobody asking), so a miner's agapite counts at ×0.1 until a smith reaches 90 Blacksmithy and asks for it (`BotBullion` orders `BotAnvil.Best`/`Plentiful(able)`): by design — Patrick's "do not flood" — but it is the one place this touches a gatherer's levelling; if `Balance:` shows coloured ingots at the floor for hours and nobody mines, `dial BotGlut.Tolerance 40` or disable. (4) `Scrap` is learned only from peddles that happen; before the first peddle the surplus price is the factor's, which is lower than the counter would pay — self-correcting as the first loads sell. (5) The factor is cached five seconds per kind and read on every appraisal of every maker's offer; `Showing` walks ≤ 24 open shops and `Asked` ≤ 512 wants per read — fine at 210 bots.
- *Status:* attempt.
- *Code:* `BotMarket/BotGlut.cs` (new); `BotMarket/BotMarket.cs` (`Traded` → `BotGlut.Sold`, `Reset`); `BotMarket/BotMarketConfig.cs`; `BotCraft/BotCraftwork.cs` (`Produced` → `BotGlut.Made`, `Choose`); `BotCraft/BotThread.cs` (`Choose`); `BotCraft/BotForge.cs`, `BotSmith.cs`, `BotSew.cs`, `BotTailor.cs`, `BotTinker.cs`, `BotTinkerer.cs`, `BotBowyer.cs`, `BotBrew.cs`, `BotAlchemist.cs`, `BotFletch.cs`, `BotFletcher.cs`, `BotBake.cs`, `BotWeave.cs`; `BotSpells/BotInscribe.cs`; `BotHarvest/BotDig.cs` (smelt booked by metal), `BotHarvest/BotChop.cs`; `BotShops/BotShops.cs` (`Sell` → `BotGlut.Peddled`); `BotPopulation/BotBeat.cs` (the `Balance:` line); `BotMarket/README.md`.

**01.10.2026 · build 385 (written by Fable) · Coloured metals: the craft path works, the engine's skill floor and the birth skill are what close it**
- *Patrick, 01.10.2026 (night plan v2, point 2):* check again that crafters can make armour from the other metals; this matters.
- *What the code does (read, not changed):* every blacksmithing recipe names `IronIngot` as its resource and the metal is chosen at the swing: `BotAnvil.Best(bot, need)` walks `DefBlacksmithy.CraftSubRes` and takes the dearest metal the pack holds enough of **and whose `RequiredSkill` is at or under the bot's Blacksmithy base** (`BotAnvil.Able`, the engine's own test at `CraftItem.cs:647`, "you cannot work this strange and unusual metal"); `BotForge.Working` asks it every beat for a round's worth, then a piece's worth, and `BotAnvil.Swing(body, recipe, tool, metal)` → `CraftItem.Craft(from, system, typeRes, tool)` — the engine maps the recipe's iron to `typeRes` in `ConsumeRes` (`CraftItem.cs:641`) and stamps the piece's `Resource`. `BotSmith.Propose` and `Order` count any workable metal (`Ingots(body, Best(body, cost))`), `BotAnvil.Keep` keeps every workable metal out of the porter's hands, `BotBullion` orders `Best`/`Plentiful(able)` rather than iron, and the skill chance is the same for every metal (`GetSuccessChance` reads the main skill only). So a smith that *can* work a coloured ingot it holds *does*, and prefers it.
- *What closes it:* the engine's floors are dull copper 65, shadow iron 70, copper 75, bronze 80, gold 85, agapite 90, verite 95, valorite 99 (base skill), and a crafter is born with `BotMobile.StartingAllowance` = 50 / 30 / 20 on its three highest targets — Blacksmithy at 30 (Mining is its highest target) — so no smith can touch a coloured bar until it has trained 35 points at the anvil, and `BotCraftwork.Margin` keeps its work five points under that again. On build 384 the shops showed 622 coloured ingots against 323 iron and no smith had the base for any of them: the bars were dug, smelted, shown and never worked. Not a defect in the craft path; a birth-skill fact, which is point 7 of the same plan (the Opus agent varying birth skills: "crafters put the most into Blacksmithy"). With Blacksmithy born at 65–70 the first coloured helm comes off the anvil on the first stint that holds the metal; nothing else needs changing.
- *One thing to keep in mind for that agent:* `BotAnvil.Able` reads `Skills[Blacksmith].Base`, so a birth value set through `Skills[].Base` (as `BotMobile` does) opens the metals at once; a value that only lifts `Value` (a hammer's bonus, a stat) does not.
- *Status:* finding; no code change. The balance entry above prices the unworkable coloured bars as the glut they are until a smith can ask for them.

Fills by kind: Leather 369 (1,817gp), Iron Ingot 365 (1,361gp), Raw Ribs 210, Feather 157, Log 40, leather and plate armour ~100 pieces (~4,000gp). Wants said: Raw Ribs 1,166 units, Leather 450, Iron Ingot 380, Feather 166. Restocks bought "off the market" from anywhere: Arrow 321, Sulfurous Ash 262, Black Pearl 137, Cloth 110, cure and heal potions 143 (1,500gp). Against that the bots' shops by the banks made 20 sales for 526gp; 57 shifts opened, 32 of the 45 that ended sold nothing. 15,958 things of 17 kinds sat under the 2gp floor.

- *Why:* the auction was trade without a place: a miner at a seam in Minoc filled a tailor's want in Yew in one line of arithmetic, a hunter's leather reached a bench it never walked to, a bot restocked arrows "off the market" standing in a dungeon. Every chain the shard has (leather, ore → ingots → armour, logs and feathers → arrows and bows, reagents → potions and scrolls, cloth → bandages, meat → cooked) ran through it, so removing it means giving each chain a road that walks.
- *Decision — the market (`BotMarket/`, module `Market`, phase World, requires Will; `BotAuction/` deleted with its stalls, escrow, fills, crossing, fetches, haggling, levy and `bot-auction.json`):*
  - `BotMarket` keeps the spoken wants and the learned prices. `Ask` holds no gold: a bot says what it wants at what price if it could pay for one out of pack and bank (`Unfunded` otherwise), in the world's chat (`market:want`), again every `SayWantMs` (2 min) while open; unanswered for `RaiseMs` it asks `RaiseStep` louder (`market:raise`) up to ×`MostMultiple` if the buyer can pay the louder price, and gives up at the ceiling (`Abandoned`); a want whose buyer can no longer pay for one is stood down by the beat (`Unpaid`). `Worth` = best open offer (capped at ×`MostMultiple` of the fallback), else the average of what really changed hands (`Traded`), else the fallback. The money order is the auction's: `Charge` (pack coin first, then the account, all or nothing) → goods move → `Refund` what did not move (coin back to the pack as far as coin came out of it) → `Pay` the seller in coin into its pack. No levy.
  - `BotHandover.Exchange` is the only way goods pass between two bots: both alive, same map, within `MeetTiles` 2; merchandise from the seller's pack (never bound kit), coin pack to pack; says `market:hand`/`market:paid` locally; posts a `market` event; `BotRegard.Traded` and `BotBurgh.Supplied` as sales did.
  - `BotCourier` (proposer "Courier", Free rung) offers a bot holding what somebody wants — in its pack, or in its bank box when it stands at a bank — the walk to the buyer within `Reach` 400 tiles, on the same land (`BotGates.Joined`), not sealed by its ledger, worth `LeastGold` 8gp or more; claim = gold ×1.25 for a pact partner, over walk + half a minute. `BotDeliver` ("deliver", steadfast) reserves the units on the want (`BotWant.Reserve`, swept when the carrier is on other work), says `market:bring` to the world, follows the buyer (walk order by Mobile, not by point) and hands over within 2 tiles; gives up after `GiveUpMs` 8 minutes of walking (`Late`). The buyer's coin at a delivery is booked aside (`BotYield.Aside`) so its own hunt does not learn that hunting loses money; `BotYield.Standing` is plain wealth now (a want holds no gold).
  - Nothing is put out from a bench, seam, corpse or field. Trade endings count what a want waits for (`BotMarket.Answering`, "for an order") and keep the goods. The porter (`BotUnload`) keeps in the pack what a want within a carrier's reach asks for — capped at what the island asks for (`BotMarket.Holding`), so one want for five bandages does not keep six hundred — and banks the rest. The miner does the same with ingots (`BotDig.Store`). A bot reaches its own bank box only standing at a bank (`BotMarket.FromBank`, counter `BoxTaken`) — the crafts' "take my own stuff back off the market" became this.
  - `BotOrder` (the maker's errand for an order) holds no escrow; `BotStores`, `BotBullion`, `BotUpkeep`, `BotAcquire`, `BotSeeker`/`BotArmoury` say wants aloud instead of lodging gold.
  - `BotCity` moved to `BotMarket/` (store format unchanged): its buys, fairs and standing orders are served at the bots' open shops (`BotShopkeep.CityBuy`), not off stalls.
  - `BotHand.ResetPopulation` → `BotMarket.Reset` (wants, prices, reservations, handover/courier/delivery counters). Dashboard gump Market tab lists the shops' lots; web JSON `wants[]` keeps `lodged` (0) and adds `coming`.
- *Watch:* `The market:` — wants said / met / given up / unfunded / unpaid / raised; `handed over against wants`; the meetings (moved, coin against cheque, refusals by cause: apart, broke, empty, pack full, absent); the carriers (looks, carrying, offered, from the box; passed over: far, unjoined, sealed, broke, petty, covered); the deliveries (taken, handed over, tiles, failed: buyer gone/dead, other land, answered first, unloaded, late, refused, blocked). Healthy: deliveries handed over ≫ late + refused; "wants met" of the order of the old fills for Leather, Iron Ingot, Raw Ribs, Feather. If "met" collapses while "carrying" is high, deliveries are losing to other work in the appraisal (raise `BotCourier.LeastClaim`, never the price).
